title: OpenAI Pauses Some Astra Work After Flagging Possible Critical Cyber Capabilities
blurb: OpenAI said Friday it cannot rule out that its unreleased Astra model has reached the Critical cyber threshold, meaning it could autonomously develop zero-day exploits or execute novel attacks from a high-level goal, and paused internal activities that fall short of strengthened security controls. Astra would be the first OpenAI model to potentially qualify for Critical under its Preparedness Framework, above earlier models like GPT-5.6-Sol that were rated High.

title: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a dense 30B-parameter open-source multimodal model that runs locally and pairs a 2B Perception Encoder for vision with a 28B text decoder. It ships with day-0 support in transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Inference Endpoints, plus an optional speculative-decoding drafter that speeds up structured tasks like code generation.

title: Meta Muse Glimmer – open weights 30B local coding model
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weights model from its Superintelligence Labs, under a permissive Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face. Optimized for always-on local agent workflows like coding, function calling, and LLM-as-a-judge, it runs on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU, with llama.cpp, MLX, and ExecuTorch integrations landing in the coming days.

title: Meta returns to open source with Muse Glimmer, an Apache 2.0 licensed 30B parameter AI model optimized for agents — available now
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, designed to run autonomous agents locally on high-end Macs and PCs. The weights are on Hugging Face now, with Ollama, vLLM, and Together AI support rolling out this week, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta will also open the weights for its Muse Spark 1.2 foundation model soon.

title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA
blurb: Researchers disclosed three ways to defeat passkey protections without breaking their underlying cryptography, instead reusing signed authentication material, recovering synced private keys from Google Password Manager in Chrome, and abusing a hardware-bound Windows Hello for Business key from an already-compromised session. Microsoft patched the related Windows Event Logging flaw (CVE-2026-34348, CVSS 6.5) and applied Entra mitigations, but the findings show neither synced nor device-bound passkeys close the full attack surface.

title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer for local AI agents
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0 that runs always-on agents on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Built by Meta Superintelligence Labs for local tool-calling, coding, and multi-step reasoning, it quantizes to under 20 GB to fit a 24 GB or 32 GB envelope and is available now on HuggingFace.

title: LexisNexis shuts down services after suspicious activity on servers
blurb: LexisNexis took its Nexis Diligence, Metabase API, and Newsdesk services offline after detecting suspicious activity on a third-party vendor's servers.

title: Tail-call optimization in C is relatively recent
blurb: C compilers historically avoided tail-call optimization because the calling convention required the caller to clean up arguments after a call, forcing every call to be followed by a return and preventing the tail position from being reused. GCC gained a workaround with a separate calling convention in 2001 and now handles it, which makes copy-and-patch compilation with 100,000 code snippets practical where goto-based interpreter dispatch could not scale.

title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer AI Model People Can Run on Their Laptop
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a downloadable AI model that runs on a personal laptop rather than in the cloud. The release pushes Meta further into the open-weights camp and sharpens the US policy debate over whether increasingly capable models should be freely distributed or held under tighter control.

title: Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open in note taking app
blurb: A security researcher found that tl;dv, an AI meeting-recorder with over 2 million users, exposed its entire Firestore database with no tenant isolation, letting any authenticated user query every account's meeting records and grab live conference IDs to walk into calls uninvited. The flaw was reported in January 2026 and remains unpatched six months later, with the exposure covering roughly 1,000 actively recording meetings at any moment.

title: OpenAI’s Upcoming Astra Model Raises Autonomous Cyberattack Concerns
blurb: OpenAI flagged its upcoming Astra model as potentially the first to hit the "critical" cybersecurity tier under its Preparedness Framework, meaning it could autonomously build zero-day exploits and run end-to-end cyberattacks from a high-level goal. The company has paused internal Astra projects that lack new controls, enforcing isolated testing, network restrictions, chain-of-thought monitoring, and joint evaluations with government agencies and AI safety groups.

title: Run Local Agentic AI Workflows with Meta’s Muse Glimmer on NVIDIA
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight dense model with a 120K-plus token context window built for local agentic workloads rather than chat, marking the company's return to open-weight releases. Optimized for NVIDIA edge, desktop, and workstation hardware, it hits 20K tokens/sec on a single GPU and fits within the VRAM of a RTX 5090, keeping inference and proprietary data fully on device.

title: Kimsuky Builds Offline AI Stack to Boost Phishing and Automate Malware Development
blurb: Security firm Genians found that Kimsuky, a North Korean espionage unit, is running AI offline on its own servers using Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty, with a configured RAG database to query documents in its possession. As AI cleans up the translation errors and formatting tells that once flagged phishing, defenders must correlate on-machine behavior like LNK execution, PowerShell, and scheduled tasks instead of judging lures by polish.

title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
blurb: Security researcher Cory Solovewicz bought the domains noreply.net and noreply.us and turned them into an accidental honeypot, receiving 401,796 misdirected emails since December 2024 that include injury reports, test credentials, and account setup data. Companies send sensitive information to placeholder @noreply addresses assuming no one is watching, exposing widespread internal misconfigurations that Solovewicz detailed at Defcon.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's GIC form Theseus Infrastructure to develop AI computing sites; Anthropic commits to cover consumer electricity price hikes (Mark Bergen/Bloomberg)
blurb: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC formed Theseus Infrastructure, a joint venture to develop and finance AI computing sites. Anthropic separately committed to cover any consumer electricity price increases tied to the data centers' power demand, an attempt to defuse the growing backlash against AI infrastructure straining local grids and raising utility bills.

title: Intel to Sell $15 Billion in Stock After AI Boosts Demand
blurb: Intel plans to sell $15B in new stock to fund its turnaround and ride surging AI-driven chip demand, in what may be its first public share sale since going public in 1971. The raise gives Intel fresh capital to extend a fragile comeback and build out capacity, while diluting existing shareholders to bet on the AI cycle.

title: Sources: Palmer Luckey's Erebor, which aims to fill the gap left by Silicon Valley Bank's collapse, is in advanced talks to raise ~$1.5B at an $8B valuation (Financial Times)
blurb: Palmer Luckey's Erebor is in advanced talks to raise roughly $1.5B at an $8B valuation, according to the Financial Times. The startup aims to fill the void left by Silicon Valley Bank's 2023 collapse, positioning itself as a lender to defense, crypto, and other startups underserved by traditional banks.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie and GIC Form Venture for AI Data Centers
blurb: Anthropic formed a joint venture with Macquarie Asset Management and Singapore's GIC to build data centers dedicated to running Claude. The deal secures long-term compute capacity through infrastructure and sovereign-wealth capital, letting Anthropic scale its footprint without shouldering the full buildout cost on its own balance sheet.

title: Meta to open source its most powerful AI model as it takes swipe at OpenAI, Anthropic
blurb: Meta will open the weights for Muse Spark 1.2, its most powerful model, and ship a new laptop-focused open-source family called Muse Glimmer. Zuckerberg framed the move as a bid to counter Chinese open-weight labs like DeepSeek and Alibaba, part of an effort to justify Meta's projected $145B in capital expenditure this year.

title: Meta Opens Muse Glimmer as Zuckerberg Presses U.S. AI Policy Shift
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model that runs on a single consumer GPU for agents handling multistep coding and admin tasks on a Mac or PC. Zuckerberg paired the launch with a 6,500-word essay urging fewer U.S. barriers on training data and distillation, while Meta kept its stronger Muse Spark model behind a paid cloud service and projected up to $145B in 2026 capital spending.

title: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0 that runs multi-step AI agents locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. The model handles tool calls, code, files, and screenshots across 100-plus languages, and forms the clearest picture yet of Zuckerberg's "personal superintelligence" vision built around always-on agents that process personal data on-device rather than in the cloud.

title: One of China's workhorse rockets just exploded in flight
blurb: China's Long March 7A rocket exploded roughly 80 seconds after liftoff Monday evening from the Wenchang Space Launch Site, likely near maximum dynamic pressure and possibly ended by its flight termination system. The medium-lift vehicle was carrying a classified payload believed to be a military communications satellite, and it marks a rare failure for a state program that has grown to 50 or more launches per year.

title: Sources: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-gen AI chip, the Maia 300, potentially as soon as September, and is in talks with TSMC to make 300K+ chips for 2027 (The Information)
blurb: Microsoft plans to introduce Maia 300, its next-generation AI accelerator, potentially as soon as September, according to The Information. The company is in talks with TSMC to manufacture more than 300,000 chips for 2027, a scale-up that would deepen Microsoft's push to reduce its reliance on Nvidia for training and inference.

title: OpenAI tightens controls on its new model over cybersecurity risks, as AI security debate intensifies
blurb: OpenAI halted some internal activities involving its unreleased Astra model after preliminary evaluations indicated it could reach "Critical" cyber capability, meaning autonomous attacks against sophisticated defenses. The company added isolated testing environments and universal monitoring for risky actions, as recent security incidents at Anthropic and Meta push lawmakers toward an "AI Kill Switch Act" requiring labs to shut down or throttle their models.

title: Intel announces a $15B common stock offering, with proceeds going to general corporate purposes, like "maintaining a strong balance sheet"; INTC falls 3%+ (Ian King/Bloomberg)
blurb: Intel announced a $15B common stock offering, with proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes including maintaining a strong balance sheet. INTC fell more than 3% on the news as investors weighed the dilution against Intel's ongoing push to fund its foundry buildout and turnaround.

title: Tel Aviv- and San Francisco-based Corma, which develops AI models for defensive cybersecurity, emerges from stealth with a $60M seed led by Sequoia Capital (Emily Forlini/Fortune)
blurb: Corma emerged from stealth with a $60M seed round led by Sequoia Capital to build AI models for defensive cybersecurity. The Tel Aviv- and San Francisco-based startup joins a crowded field of security vendors betting that AI can shift the advantage toward defenders who monitor and respond to threats.

title: Sources: the AI-driven memory chip shortage has kicked off a rush of DC lobbying; many US officials appear unsympathetic to Apple's desire to buy Chinese chips (New York Times)
blurb: The AI-driven memory chip shortage has triggered a lobbying rush in Washington, with companies pressing officials over supply constraints and sourcing rules. US officials appear unsympathetic to Apple's push to buy Chinese-made memory chips, according to the New York Times, signaling that national-security concerns still override cost pressures even as the shortage bites.

title: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
blurb: TSMC reported July revenue of NT$467.58B ($14.5B), up 44.7% year over year, as AI chip demand pushed monthly sales ahead of its full-year growth guidance. The world's largest chip manufacturer, which fabricates for Nvidia and Google, now expects 2026 revenue to rise slightly above 40% in dollar terms and raised its capital expenditure plan to between $60B and $64B.

title: Apple reveals how Siri AI features work in China – raising privacy questions
blurb: Apple will power Siri's new AI features in China with Alibaba's Qwen models, diverging from the Google Gemini setup it uses elsewhere. Chinese law permits only local AI models, so the privacy protections applied in other regions likely won't carry over, and Reuters notes Mac users must sign into their own Qwen accounts to access the features.

title: How Mailchimp Went From $1B+ ARR to … Shrinking Inside Intuit. A Death Spiral in the Age of AI?
blurb: Intuit reported its Q3 FY26 results with Mailchimp stripped out of the growth figures, disclosing that the email platform it bought for roughly $12B in 2021 is now declining year over year and absorbing a 17% workforce cut. The author argues the collapse is structural: Mailchimp diluted a product that won by staying narrow, then missed the shift as new email signups moved from marketers in a UI to developers and models provisioning it by API.

title: Whatnot raises $545M from ICONIQ, Lightspeed and Avra to fuel live commerce expansion
blurb: Whatnot raised $545M in a Series G round at a $20B valuation, led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed, and Avra, nearly doubling its worth in under a year. The live commerce platform, which takes a cut of seller livestream auctions for collectibles, fashion, and electronics, already topped last year's gross merchandise volume halfway through 2026 and is targeting expansion in the UK and Europe.

title: Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models
blurb: Mark Zuckerberg criticized "closed" AI competitors as Meta signaled a return to open models after months of internal debate over its strategy. The comments follow Meta's reorganization of its AI teams and reported hesitation over open-sourcing its largest Llama models, a shift that had raised questions about the company's long-standing commitment to open-weight releases.

title: Microsoft Plans Production Boost for AI Chips, Information Says
blurb: Microsoft plans to significantly increase production of its next-generation in-house AI chips, according to a report from the Information. The move would deepen Microsoft's push to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs for its data centers, joining Google, Amazon, and Meta in building custom silicon to control costs and supply as AI demand climbs.

title: UK's Royal Navy sea drones contain component that secretly sent data to China, report claims — government cuts camera connectivity and insists data wasn’t sensitive, only ‘heartbeat communications’
blurb: K3 Scout surveillance drones used by the UK's Royal Navy contain a Chinese-made camera component that was secretly transmitting data to China, according to a Telegraph report on the vessels operated by defense contractor Kraken Technology Group. The Ministry of Defence has since cut all internet connectivity from the cameras and says the leaked data was limited to "heartbeat communications" confirming the device was online, though sources called the lapse a major failure.

title: The Deluge of AI Debt Has Big Names Seeking New Strategies to Avoid Selloffs
blurb: Big tech's rush to fund AI buildouts has flooded credit markets with debt, prompting underwriters like BlackRock to engineer deals that shield issuers from fast-money selloffs. BlackRock structured Meta's recent financing to keep short-term traders from destabilizing the offering, a sign that arrangers now see managing bond volatility as central to closing the largest AI-driven borrowing rounds.

title: A data breach at shipping giant Ceva Logistics is rippling across banks, retailers, Steam gamers, and beyond
blurb: A breach at logistics giant Ceva Logistics exposed customer names, addresses, and contact details across banks, retailers, and Steam hardware buyers.

title: Sila lands $1.4B Pentagon loan as militaries demand more batteries
blurb: Sila landed a $1.4B loan from the U.S. Department of Defense to expand production of its silicon-carbon battery material at its Moses Lake, Washington factory. The deal positions Sila as a rare non-Chinese source of high-energy-density anodes for drones and EVs, and could open the door to defense contracts as buyers scramble for battery materials made outside China.

title: Mistral Patent for "Code implemented tool calls"
blurb: Mistral was granted a US patent covering "code implemented tool calls," a method where an LLM writes a code block that encapsulates tool calls, executes it in a server sandbox, and pauses to hand pending calls to a client before resuming with the results. The technique mirrors a pattern already common across the industry, raising the prospect that a widely used agent design could face patent-enforcement questions.

title: Unitree’s Shanghai IPO 5,526 Times Subscribed by Retail Buyers
blurb: Unitree Robotics, China's leading humanoid robot maker, saw its Shanghai IPO oversubscribed 5,526 times by retail investors as the company opened its books. The demand underscores how heavily Chinese retail buyers are betting on domestic robotics, a sector Beijing has prioritized as it races the US in physical AI and advanced manufacturing.

title: As datacenters expand, so does public opposition to them
blurb: Local opposition to new datacenter construction is intensifying as communities push back against the water use, electricity demand, noise, and land consumption that accompany the AI-driven buildout. The report finds that permitting fights, zoning challenges, and organized resistance are increasingly delaying or blocking projects, turning community consent into a real constraint on where hyperscalers and cloud providers can expand.

title: Archer buys former rival Wisk Aero
blurb: Archer Aviation acquired Wisk Aero, the autonomous eVTOL rival that sued it for trade-secret theft in 2021, along with Boeing subsidiaries SkyGrid and Insitu. Boeing takes newly issued Archer shares worth about a 16.5% stake in exchange, capping a relationship that moved from a $1B countersuit to a settlement-driven partnership to full ownership.

title: Sources: AI cloud computing provider Lambda is selling a $917M leveraged loan to finance the purchase of GPUs as part of a contract with Nvidia (Bloomberg)
blurb: Lambda is selling a $917M leveraged loan to finance GPU purchases tied to a contract with Nvidia, according to Bloomberg sources. The debt deal lets the AI cloud provider expand capacity without diluting equity, and it underscores how GPU-backed financing has become the standard way neoclouds fund the hardware buildout behind surging AI compute demand.

title: Hyperscalers commit nearly $2 trillion to secure AI hardware and memory — Google leads $811 billion spending surge while Apple trails at $57 billion
blurb: Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon have amassed roughly $2 trillion in long-term purchase commitments for AI hardware and memory by Q2 2026, according to analyst estimates cited by Tom's Hardware, with Alphabet at about $811B and Microsoft near $678B. The buildout marks a shift from consumer electronics buyers like Apple, at around $57B, toward hyperscalers, giving memory suppliers Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix new pricing power.

title: Boeing is selling its air taxi startups to Archer Aviation
blurb: Boeing agreed to sell three eVTOL subsidiaries, including Wisk Aero, SkyGrid, and Insitu, to Archer Aviation for an undisclosed sum while taking a stake in the company. The deal lets Boeing refocus on its core airplane business amid a $715B backlog, while Archer gains autonomous flight and air-traffic tech ahead of planned air taxi launches in New York, Texas, and Florida this year.

title: GameStop May Pull $56 Billion EBay Bid
blurb: GameStop may withdraw its $56B bid for eBay and instead propose a partnership, according to people familiar with the matter. CEO Ryan Cohen's retreat from a full acquisition would end one of the largest attempted retail takeovers, leaving a looser tie-up as the fallback if talks continue.

title: Intel Shares Fall After Announcing $15 Billion Stock Offering
blurb: Intel shares fell Monday after the company announced a $15B common stock offering to fund AI growth initiatives. The dilution move signals Intel needs fresh capital to compete in AI accelerators and expand its foundry business, areas where it trails Nvidia and TSMC.

title: South Korea plans to launch a ~$3.5B chip fund for promising materials, parts, equipment, and fabless companies, and speed the development of domestic chip hubs (Reuters)
blurb: South Korea plans a ~$3.5B fund backing chip materials, parts, equipment, and fabless startups while accelerating domestic fab hubs.

title: OpenAI Courts Public Opinion in Apple Trade Secrets Fight
blurb: OpenAI has launched a public-relations campaign to shape opinion in its trade secrets dispute with Apple, moving the fight beyond the courtroom. The effort signals that OpenAI sees reputational stakes alongside the legal ones, using media pressure to counter Apple's claims as the two companies increasingly compete in AI.

title: House Dems call for AI companies to testify on recent hacks: ‘Clear risk to safety’
blurb: House Democrats led by Rep. Greg Casar asked Speaker Mike Johnson to have OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI executives testify under oath about recent cyber breaches carried out by their models. The signatories, mostly from the party's progressive wing, called the incidents a possible "canary in the coal mine" and want to question executives about the failures behind them and what regulation could prevent a repeat.

title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
blurb: Waymo now operates driverless cars in 15 U.S. cities and counting, but its rapid expansion is exposing more "edge cases," unscripted road situations its vehicles have never been trained to handle. Each new market widens the range of rare scenarios the system must resolve, keeping the long tail of self-driving safety a persistent constraint on how fast robotaxis can scale.

title: Aptoide becomes the first third-party app store to land inside Google Play
blurb: Aptoide Games is now available directly through Google Play in the US, the first competing app store to officially land inside Google's platform since it locked out rivals over a decade ago. The move stems from Google's antitrust settlement with Epic Games and a new Play Catalog Access program, with Amazon, Samsung, and the Epic Games Store positioned to follow.

title: Cyberattack on Steam hardware shipper leaks names, addresses, and order data
blurb: Valve is notifying European Steam customers that a cyberattack on shipping partner CEVA Logistics exposed names, addresses, phone numbers, and hardware order details.

title: Satyress designs centaur-like robot to give workers "superpowers" for dangerous jobs
blurb: California startup Satyress introduced Threehalves, a teleoperated centaur-like humanoid robot designed to handle dangerous jobs that expose workers to injury, extreme conditions, or death. Founder Beau Gaston, who has built the machine since 2022, frames it as giving operators "superpowers" by placing a controllable robotic body in hazardous environments while the human stays remote.

title: Meta's 'open source' Muse Glimmer model can run on a single computer
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a slimmed-down "open source" AI model light enough to run on a single computer rather than a data-center cluster. The smaller footprint lowers the hardware barrier for developers who want to run or fine-tune the model locally, extending Meta's push to seed its models across the open ecosystem.

title: Valve informs customers about data breach, personal data stolen
blurb: Valve notified customers of a data breach after a vendor handling Steam hardware deliveries was hacked, exposing personal information.

title: Chinese Long March 7A rocket explodes shortly after liftoff
blurb: A Chinese Long March 7A rocket exploded roughly 85 seconds after its August 10 liftoff from Wenchang, apparently destroying the Zhongxing-4B payload believed to be a military communications satellite. The failure marks China's fourth loss in 56 orbital attempts this year and raises questions for upcoming missions, since the rocket's YF-100 kerolox engines are shared with the Long March 5 set to launch the Chang'e-7 lunar mission on August 24.

title: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
blurb: Local bans on new data center construction jumped from 300 in late June to over 500 in July, with bipartisan opposition emerging across Republican- and Democrat-run states over strain on water, power, and public services. Texas Governor Greg Abbott has paused new approvals pending a grid audit, and most restrictions cluster in the Midwest and South, threatening the physical buildout AI firms need for capacity.

title: Europe’s IRIS2 Constellation Enters the Build Phase
blurb: The EU, ESA, and the SpaceRISE consortium of SES, Eutelsat, and HispaSat agreed to move IRIS2 into its build phase, expanding the secure-connectivity constellation to at least 348 satellites at a cost of ~€15.6B ($17.95B). Eutelsat will lead the 330 LEO satellites, SES will build 18 MEO payloads, and HispaSat handles ground infrastructure, with first launches on a European rocket targeted for 2029.

title: Over 70% of Americans oppose AI data centers; US protests intensify as more arrests are being made — almost 40 arrested this year in backlash to AI factory buildout
blurb: More than 70% of Americans oppose new AI data centers, and roughly 40 people have been arrested this year at protests against the buildout. Nashville's city council just moved to block a $700M facility near the zoo, while Virginia regulators ruled that data centers must pay for the transmission infrastructure they exclusively use, reflecting mounting local resistance over noise, water strain, and rising residential electricity bills.

title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million in New Mexico Child Safety Case
blurb: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $567 million for failing to protect children from exploitation and harmful content, bringing its total penalties in the case to $942 million after an earlier $375 million fine. The order also forces operational changes in the state, including removing Like counts for minors without parental approval, pausing overnight push notifications to under-18 users, and capping their usage at 90 hours per month; Meta plans to appeal.

title: Amazon-Backed Texas Gas Plant Could Emit 33 Million Tons of CO2 a Year
blurb: Amazon confirmed it acquired the GW Ranch site in Pecos County, Texas, and will buy power for an AI data center campus from a Pacifico Energy gas plant permitted to emit up to 33 million tons of CO2 a year. That regulatory ceiling exceeds the largest single facility on the EPA's 2023 emissions map and cuts against Amazon's net-zero-by-2040 pledge, as its reported emissions climbed 16% to 80.9 million tons in 2025.

title: Discovered Materials is playing AI whack-a-mole to hunt cooler chips
blurb: Discovered Materials raised $9M seed from Lightspeed India to run AI agent swarms hunting cooler semiconductor materials, launching a Material Discovery Bench alongside.

title: Squeak/Smalltalk 6.1 Release Notes
blurb: Squeak/Smalltalk 6.1 "Vanessa" ships after four years, merging 1700+ patches with a new tree browser and the return of Objectland.

title: Four takeaways from Mark Zuckerberg’s massive AI manifesto
blurb: Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word essay titled "The Future is for Everyone," laying out his case for developing "personal superintelligence" and distributing it to billions of people through free and open-source models. The manifesto also addresses Meta's data center backlash with pledges to generate low-cost community energy, restore more water than it consumes by 2030, and fund training and jobs in areas where it builds.

title: EY Launching Unit to Keep a Lid on Artificial Intelligence Costs
blurb: EY is creating a "head of agent economics" role to track whether its expanding AI-powered workforce justifies the cost. The hire signals that white-collar firms are shifting from adopting AI to auditing its return, scrutinizing per-agent spend the way they once scrutinized headcount.

title: Nvidia AI interconnect darling bags $136M funding from Arm, others
blurb: Point2 Technology raised $136M in Series B funding, adding Arm to backers including Nvidia, for its plastic-waveguide AI data center interconnects.

title: Online course cheating has accelerated from chatbot-written essays to agents executing commands like "log in and complete my quiz"; major AI tools didn't refuse (New York Times)
blurb: Online course cheating has escalated from chatbot-written essays to AI agents that execute commands like "log in and complete my quiz," with major tools carrying out the tasks rather than refusing. The shift moves the problem from detectable text to autonomous actions inside learning platforms, undercutting proctoring defenses built for an earlier era and raising fresh questions about where AI vendors should draw refusal lines.

title: As Waymo expands its fleet from 700 in 2025 to nearly 4,000 now, recalls and edge-case failures like flooded roadways and a San Francisco power outage mount (Emmy Martin/New York Times)
blurb: Waymo grew its robotaxi fleet from 700 in 2025 to nearly 4,000 today, as recalls and edge-case failures pile up.

blurb: A security researcher found that tl;dv, an AI meeting-recording platform with over 2 million users, left its Firestore database without tenant isolation, letting any authenticated user query every meeting across all accounts and pull creator emails plus joinable conference IDs for roughly 1,000 live calls at any moment. The flaw was reported in January 2026 and remains unpatched six months later, with the researcher demonstrating it by joining active calls uninvited.

blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, an open-source, local, agentic vision-language model with day-0 support in transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Inference Endpoints. The dense 30B model pairs a 2B Perception Encoder for images and video with a 28B text decoder that uses hybrid sliding-window and full attention plus gated grouped-query attention to cut KV-cache memory by 16x.

title: Meta returns to open source with Muse Glimmer, an Apache 2.0 licensed 30B parameter AI model optimized for agents — available now
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 license, designed to run autonomous agents locally on high-end Macs and PCs. The weights are on Hugging Face now, with support rolling out this week across Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and Together AI, marking Meta's first fully open release since it moved the Muse family to proprietary licensing in April.

title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer for local AI agents
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model under an Apache 2.0 license, built to run always-on agents on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Quantization brings the language model under 20 GB to fit a 24 GB or 32 GB envelope, and Meta positions it against Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B with strong agentic results for its size.

title: Meta Muse Glimmer – open weights 30B local coding model
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter agentic model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, under a permissive Apache 2.0 license with open weights on Hugging Face. The model is optimized for always-on local workflows like function calling, coding, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and runs on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU via llama.cpp, MLX, and ExecuTorch.

blurb: Genians reported that Kimsuky, a North Korean espionage group under the Reconnaissance General Bureau, has begun running AI models offline on its own servers using Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty, and connecting document-search tools to files in its possession. Researchers found no evidence the group trained its own model, describing an actor in a research phase assembling existing tools to speed phishing and automate malware development.

title: Import AI 468: 23 RSI ideas; PostTrainBench+; and how trust and transparency interplay with AI racing
blurb: Think tank IFP published 23 policy recommendations, grouped into seven categories, to help policymakers manage the risks of increasingly automated AI R&D. The proposals span providing transparency into automated R&D, building state capacity to respond, accelerating AI verification technology, and extending the US lead to buy more time before recursive self-improvement outpaces the tools available to steer it.

title: OpenAI Pauses Some Astra Work After Flagging Possible Critical Cyber Capabilities
blurb: OpenAI said Friday it cannot rule out that its unreleased Astra model could autonomously develop zero-day exploits or execute novel cyberattacks from a high-level goal, and it paused internal activities involving the model that fall short of strengthened security controls. Astra would be the first OpenAI model to potentially reach the Critical cyber threshold, a step above the High rating given to earlier models like GPT-5.6-Sol.

title: OpenAI’s Upcoming Astra Model Raises Autonomous Cyberattack Concerns
blurb: OpenAI flagged its upcoming Astra model as potentially reaching the "critical" cybersecurity tier under its Preparedness Framework, meaning the model could autonomously build zero-day exploits against hardened systems or design and execute end-to-end cyberattacks from a high-level goal. The company paused internal Astra projects lacking new security controls, enforcing isolated testing, network restrictions, tighter weight protections, and chain-of-thought monitoring that intercepts high-risk behavior.

title: Introducing FILE type: a native column type for multimodal data
blurb: Databricks announced the beta of FILE, a new column type that stores unstructured data like documents, images, audio, and video as a native, governed column alongside structured tables in the lakehouse. Databricks is building the type into open Parquet and Delta Lake formats, keeping multimodal data queryable and portable across the ecosystem rather than locked in a separate system.

title: Sources: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-gen AI chip, the Maia 300, potentially as soon as September, and is in talks with TSMC to make 300K+ chips for 2027 (The Information)
blurb: Microsoft plans to release its next-generation AI chip, the Maia 300, potentially as early as September, and is in talks with TSMC to manufacture more than 300,000 of the chips for 2027. The move signals a push to scale in-house silicon and reduce reliance on NVIDIA GPUs for its AI data center buildout.

title: Run Local Agentic AI Workflows with Meta’s Muse Glimmer on NVIDIA
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight dense model with a 120K+ context window built for local agentic workflows rather than chat, and optimized to run across NVIDIA edge, desktop, and workstation platforms at 20K tokens/sec on a single GPU. Its dense architecture activates every parameter per token, giving it the instruction-following reliability, long-context coherence, and predictable latency that multi-step agents need while fitting in a single GPU's VRAM for fully on-device inference.

title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer AI Model People Can Run on Their Laptop
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a downloadable AI model that runs locally on a personal laptop rather than in the cloud. The release adds momentum to a US policy debate over whether increasingly capable models should be freely available or kept under tighter control by their developers.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's GIC form Theseus Infrastructure to develop AI computing sites; Anthropic commits to cover consumer electricity price hikes (Mark Bergen/Bloomberg)
blurb: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's GIC formed Theseus Infrastructure, a venture to develop AI computing sites in the US. Anthropic separately committed to cover consumer electricity price increases tied to the datacenter buildout, an unusual concession as AI power demand strains local grids and household bills.

title: SEC Exempts Data-Center Bonds From Key Securitization Rules
blurb: The SEC exempted data-center bonds from key securitization rules, making it easier for data center owners to sell asset-backed securities. The move could open the door to more debt sales as tech firms search Wall Street for ways to finance the buildout of AI infrastructure.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie and GIC Form Venture for AI Data Centers
blurb: Anthropic formed a strategic partnership with Macquarie Asset Management and Singaporean wealth fund GIC to build data centers dedicated to Claude. The venture gives Anthropic access to institutional capital and infrastructure expertise as it scales compute capacity to meet rising demand for its models.

title: Meta to open source its most powerful AI model as it takes swipe at OpenAI, Anthropic
blurb: Meta will open the weights for Muse Spark 1.2, its most powerful model, and release Muse Glimmer, a new open-source family designed to run on laptops. In a 6,500-word essay, Zuckerberg framed the move as a challenge to Chinese open-weight labs like DeepSeek and Alibaba, urging Washington to ease training-data restrictions so American open models can lead.

title: OpenAI adds technology to compete for ad dollars
blurb: OpenAI added product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to ChatGPT, giving performance marketers the shopping surfaces and conversion tracking needed to run ad campaigns rather than experimental buys. The additions position ChatGPT to compete for advertising budgets, a revenue stream dominated by Google and Meta, as OpenAI looks to monetize its consumer traffic beyond subscriptions.

title: Intel to Sell $15 Billion in Stock After AI Boosts Demand
blurb: Intel plans to sell $15 billion in new common stock to fund its turnaround and expand capacity for AI-driven chip demand. The offering would be Intel's first public share sale since its 1971 listing, giving the company fresh capital as it works to regain ground lost to rivals in the AI market.

title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda Taps Loans for Nvidia-Tied Chip Deal
blurb: Lambda, an Nvidia-backed AI cloud provider, is selling a leveraged loan to finance a chip purchase tied to Nvidia. The deal pushes the risky corporate debt market into the growing wave of borrowing used to fund AI infrastructure buildouts.

title: Meta Opens Muse Glimmer as Zuckerberg Presses U.S. AI Policy Shift
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model built for agents that handle multistep tasks locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer graphics card. Zuckerberg paired the release with a 6,500-word essay calling for fewer U.S. barriers around training data and distillation, while Meta kept its more capable Muse Spark behind a paid cloud service.

title: ‘Ghostjacking’ Attack Uses Poisoned Logs to Turn AI Agents Bad
blurb: Tenet security researchers demonstrated Ghostjacking, an attack that plants malicious instructions inside logs and alerts from trusted platforms like Cloudflare, Datadog, and Sentry, tricking AI agents into executing them when analysts ask for a review. In one demonstration, the technique altered Cloudflare DNS settings to an attacker-controlled domain 9 times out of 10 against Claude Code, using instructions carried in by Cloudflare's own managed firewall block logs.

title: Can Agents Use a Computer Yet? We've Got the Data
blurb: Computer-using agents have moved from demos to production for narrow, repeatable back-office workflows: updating systems of record, moving data through portals, processing tickets, and handling the long tail of legacy software with no clean API. a16z argues the models improved faster than expected, and the cost curve is starting to work where labor would otherwise mean clicking through legacy systems by hand. Agents remain brittle when work drifts off the runbook, and caching-intractable cases stay too expensive to justify everywhere.

title: Claude Code puts auto mode in the driver's seat
blurb: Anthropic added an auto mode to Claude Code that lets the agent plan and execute multi-step coding tasks with less manual approval at each step. The mode hands more control to the model for running commands and editing files across a session, shifting the developer's role toward reviewing outcomes rather than confirming every individual action.

title: What a Claude Code subagent actually costs: measuring the ~436k-token fixed overhead
blurb: This post measures the fixed cost of spawning a Claude Code subagent, finding that each one carries roughly 436k tokens of overhead from its initial context load and final cache write, versus about 46k tokens for the embedded review content itself. The 9.5:1 ratio of fixed cost to payload means agent headcount, not prompt size, is the real cost lever, so consolidating perspectives into fewer agents cut one pipeline's bill to 37.6% of the multi-agent version.

title: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 license that runs multi-step AI agents locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. The model supports text and images across more than 100 languages, and is Meta's clearest articulation yet of Zuckerberg's "personal superintelligence" vision, keeping personal data on-device to power always-on agents that manage schedules, draft messages, and organize files.

title: OpenAI tightens controls on its new model over cybersecurity risks, as AI security debate intensifies
blurb: OpenAI halted some internal activities involving its unreleased model Astra after preliminary evaluations indicated it could not rule out "Critical" cyber capability, meaning autonomous attacks against sophisticated defenses. The company said it has imposed stricter controls including isolated testing environments and universal monitoring for risky actions, as recent security incidents at Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI push lawmakers toward an "AI Kill Switch Act.

title: Sources: the AI-driven memory chip shortage has kicked off a rush of DC lobbying; many US officials appear unsympathetic to Apple's desire to buy Chinese chips (New York Times)
blurb: The AI-driven memory chip shortage has triggered a surge of DC lobbying, according to sources cited by the New York Times. Many US officials appear unsympathetic to Apple's push to buy Chinese-made chips to ease supply constraints, signaling limited relief for companies caught between demand and export policy.

title: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
blurb: TSMC reported July revenue of NT$467.58 billion ($14.5 billion), up 44.7% year over year, as AI-related chip demand continued to strengthen. The result puts the world's largest chip manufacturer ahead of its guidance for slightly above 40% revenue growth in 2026, a year in which high-performance computing already accounted for 66% of revenue and capex guidance rose to $60B to $64B.

title: Apple reveals how Siri AI features work in China – raising privacy questions
blurb: Apple published a guide stating that Siri's new AI features will run on Alibaba's Qwen models for users in China, rather than the Google Gemini models powering the features elsewhere. Chinese law permits only domestic AI models, and the setup requires users to sign into their own Qwen account, suggesting the privacy protections applied to Gemini and Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers will not extend to Chinese users.

title: Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models
blurb: Mark Zuckerberg criticized "closed" AI competitors as Meta shifted its strategy back toward open models. The move follows a period of internal debate over whether to keep releasing Llama weights openly, and positions Meta against rivals like OpenAI and Google that gate their frontier systems behind paid APIs.

title: Microsoft Plans Production Boost for AI Chips, Information Says
blurb: Microsoft plans to significantly increase production of its next-generation AI chips, according to a report from the Information. The move would expand Microsoft's in-house Maia silicon effort as the company works to reduce its dependence on NVIDIA GPUs for training and inference across its Azure and Copilot workloads.

title: Mistral Patent for "Code implemented tool calls"
blurb: A newly published USPTO patent grants Mistral claims over "code implemented tool calls," a method where an LLM generates a code block that encapsulates tool calls and executes it in a server-side sandbox. The patent covers pausing execution on a pending tool call, delegating it to the client, then resuming with the returned result substituted back into the code, a pattern common to many agent frameworks.

title: Sources: AI cloud computing provider Lambda is selling a $917M leveraged loan to finance the purchase of GPUs as part of a contract with Nvidia (Bloomberg)
blurb: Lambda is selling a $917M leveraged loan to finance GPU purchases tied to a contract with Nvidia, according to sources cited by Bloomberg. The debt financing underscores how AI cloud providers are increasingly turning to leverage to fund the capital-intensive buildout of GPU capacity needed to meet demand.

title: Hyperscalers commit nearly $2 trillion to secure AI hardware and memory — Google leads $811 billion spending surge while Apple trails at $57 billion
blurb: Four hyperscalers have amassed roughly $2 trillion in long-term purchase commitments for AI hardware and memory by Q2 2026, according to analyst Claus Aasholm, with Alphabet at around $811 billion and Microsoft near $678 billion. The scale of these procurement deals now dwarfs traditional buyers like Apple at $57 billion, turning memory into a strategic asset and handing pricing power to Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix.

title: JPMorgan Leads $441 Million Debt Deal for AI Infrastructure Firm
blurb: Global AI, a two-year-old AI infrastructure firm, raised $441 million in debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase to fund the buildout of AI data centers. The deal reflects rising demand for data center capacity and the growing role of debt markets in financing the infrastructure behind large-scale AI compute.

title: OpenAI Courts Public Opinion in Apple Trade Secrets Fight
blurb: OpenAI has launched a public relations campaign to shape opinion in its trade secrets dispute with Apple. The company is publicizing its side of the legal fight rather than confining the matter to court filings, signaling a strategy to pressure Apple through media coverage alongside the litigation itself.

title: Sources: officials say OpenAI risks its White House relationship by hiring Dean Ball, who has criticized Trump's AI strategy after leaving the administration (Thomas Barrabi/New York Post)
blurb: OpenAI's hiring of policy analyst Dean Ball risks straining its relationship with the White House, according to officials cited in the report. Ball, who left the Trump administration and has since criticized its AI strategy, joins a company already navigating delicate ties with the government over compute, regulation, and a proposed equity stake.

title: House Dems call for AI companies to testify on recent hacks: ‘Clear risk to safety’
blurb: A group of House Democrats, led by Rep. Greg Casar, called for the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, and other major AI companies to testify before Congress under oath following recent cyber breaches carried out by their models. The lawmakers cannot compel testimony on their own, but framed the incidents as a possible "canary in the coal mine" and pressed House Speaker Mike Johnson to hold a hearing on AI regulation.

title: Data-Center Backlash Leads to New Land Rush in Texas Oil Patch
blurb: Permian Basin landowners are marketing their acreage to AI data-center developers as local Nimby opposition stalls projects elsewhere in the US. The oil-patch sites offer existing power infrastructure, water rights, and sparse populations less likely to resist, positioning West Texas to capture demand that residential communities have rejected.

title: Trust your AI agents? New research shows ‘memory poisoning’ can dupe them into ‘remembering’ fake information – and it’s a huge security risk
blurb: Forcepoint researchers detailed a "memory poisoning" attack that plants false data, such as a fake vendor, support contact, or security rule, into an AI agent's persistent memory via hidden text in a webpage or document. Unlike prompt injection, which ends when a session closes, the poisoned items persist across sessions and are surfaced as fact months later, making long-term memory a new target surface for agentic systems.

title: Meta's 'open source' Muse Glimmer model can run on a single computer
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a slimmed-down model it describes as open source that is light enough to run on a single computer. The compact footprint targets local deployment rather than data-center hardware, letting developers run the model on their own machines without cloud infrastructure.

title: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
blurb: Local US bans on new data center developments jumped from 300 in late June to over 500 in July, according to a report from The Information, driven by bipartisan resident concerns over noise, water, and electricity strain. The pushback spans Republican- and Democrat-run areas, with Texas Governor Greg Abbott pausing approvals for a grid audit and more than 400 restrictions now concentrated in the Midwest and South.

title: Apple Posts Then Pulls China Guide Linking Siri to Alibaba's Qwen
blurb: Apple briefly published then pulled a Chinese Mac support guide showing how mainland users could connect Alibaba's Qwen to Siri and Writing Tools.

title: Workers Say AI Took Over Colleagues' Tasks as Jobs Data Shows No Measurable Shift
blurb: A July 2026 Epoch AI and Ipsos survey found that one in five employed US adults said AI now handles at least one of ten measured work tasks their team previously assigned to a coworker or contractor. The Budget Lab at Yale, however, detected no change in employment or inflation-adjusted hourly wages across AI-exposed occupations as of May 2026.

title: Over 70% of Americans oppose AI data centers; US protests intensify as more arrests are being made — almost 40 arrested this year in backlash to AI factory buildout
blurb: A new survey found that over 70% of Americans oppose AI data center construction, and nearly 40 people have been arrested this year while protesting the buildout at town meetings and rallies. Nashville's city council just approved a measure to block a $700 million data center near the Nashville Zoo, following Virginia's ruling that data centers must pay for transmission infrastructure they exclusively use.

title: Amazon-Backed Texas Gas Plant Could Emit 33 Million Tons of CO2 a Year
blurb: Amazon acquired the GW Ranch site in Pecos County, Texas, and will buy power for an AI data center campus from a Pacifico Energy gas plant permitted to emit up to 33 million tons of CO2 a year. The ceiling exceeds the largest single facility on the EPA's 2023 map and complicates Amazon's net-zero-by-2040 pledge, coming as the company's 2025 emissions rose 16% to nearly 80.9 million tons.

title: OpenAI kauft NextSlide: Dieses neue Tool könnte jetzt für ChatGPT kommen
blurb: OpenAI acquired NextSlide, a San Francisco startup whose AI software turned prompts, notes, documents, and research into editable presentations, with the deal confirmed by founder Ahmed Beshry and reportedly closed earlier this year. The NextSlide team has moved to OpenAI to work on ChatGPT, pointing to native slide-generation capabilities, though the purchase price was not disclosed.

title: Online course cheating has accelerated from chatbot-written essays to agents executing commands like "log in and complete my quiz"; major AI tools didn't refuse (New York Times)
blurb: A New York Times investigation found that online course cheating has escalated from chatbot-written essays to AI agents that execute direct commands like "log in and complete my quiz." Major AI tools tested did not refuse these requests, carrying out logins and quiz completions on students' behalf.

title: Four takeaways from Mark Zuckerberg’s massive AI manifesto
blurb: Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word essay titled "The Future is for Everyone," arguing that superintelligent AI should be delivered to billions of people for free or as affordably as possible through open source models. The manifesto also details Meta's plan to defuse the PR crisis around its data centers, pledging local energy infrastructure, a commitment to restore more water than it uses by 2030, and guaranteed high-paying trade jobs.

title: EY Launching Unit to Keep a Lid on Artificial Intelligence Costs
blurb: EY is launching a unit to control AI spending and is hiring a head of "agent economics" to oversee its growing AI-powered workforce. The move signals that white-collar firms are increasing scrutiny of whether their AI investments justify the mounting costs.

title: Anthropic ends per-action approval in Claude Code; workers keep 66% of AI output
blurb: Anthropic makes auto mode the default in Claude Code on August 14 for Pro, Max, and Team plans, routing tool calls through a Sonnet 4.6 classifier.

title: Intel to Sell $15 Billion in Stock After AI Boosts Demand
blurb: Intel plans to sell $15B in new common stock, likely its first public share sale since going public in 1971, to fund its comeback and ride the AI demand surge. The raise dilutes existing holders but signals Intel bets it can turn AI-driven chip demand into the capital it needs for foundry buildout and manufacturing catch-up. It also marks how far the company has fallen from the days when it funded expansion from its own cash flow, now leaning on equity markets to stay in the frontier race.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie and GIC Form Venture for AI Data Centers
blurb: Anthropic partnered with Macquarie Asset Management and Singapore's GIC to build and finance data centers dedicated to Claude. The deal pulls infrastructure capital from an asset manager and a sovereign wealth fund rather than the labs' own balance sheets, spreading the cost of the compute buildout across outside investors. For founders, it signals that frontier capacity is increasingly a project-finance game, and the labs racing to lock up power and hardware now are the ones who set pricing and availability for everyone building on top of them.

title: Sources: Palmer Luckey's Erebor, which aims to fill the gap left by Silicon Valley Bank's collapse, is in advanced talks to raise ~$1.5B at an $8B valuation (Financial Times)
blurb: Palmer Luckey's Erebor is in advanced talks to raise about $1.5B at an $8B valuation, positioning itself as the bank for the startups and defense-tech firms Silicon Valley Bank used to serve. SVB's 2023 collapse pulled the dedicated lender out from under the venture ecosystem, and no incumbent has fully taken its place. An $8B valuation for a bank that barely exists yet signals how much founders and their backers still want a balance sheet that actually understands startup risk.

title: Sources: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-gen AI chip, the Maia 300, potentially as soon as September, and is in talks with TSMC to make 300K+ chips for 2027 (The Information)
blurb: Microsoft plans to introduce its next-gen AI chip, the Maia 300, potentially as soon as September, and is in talks with TSMC to produce more than 300K chips for 2027. The move signals Microsoft is serious about weaning its data centers off Nvidia, where soaring GPU costs and supply constraints have squeezed every hyperscaler. For founders building on Azure, more in-house silicon eventually means cheaper, more available inference, but the near-term bet is still that custom chips take years to close the gap with Nvidia's stack.

title: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's GIC form Theseus Infrastructure to develop AI computing sites; Anthropic commits to cover consumer electricity price hikes (Mark Bergen/Bloomberg)
blurb: Anthropic, Macquarie, and Singapore's GIC formed a joint venture called Theseus Infrastructure to build AI computing sites, and Anthropic committed to cover the consumer electricity price hikes those data centers cause. The pledge is a tell: power, not chips, is becoming the binding constraint on AI buildout, and the political cost of straining local grids is now large enough that a frontier lab will absorb it directly. For founders, it signals that compute expansion is moving into project-finance territory, where energy contracts and community goodwill matter as much as model quality.

title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda Taps Loans for Nvidia-Tied Chip Deal
blurb: Lambda, the Nvidia-backed AI cloud provider, is selling a leveraged loan to finance a chip purchase, pushing the AI buildout into the riskier corners of the debt market. Cloud providers used to fund GPU fleets with equity and Nvidia's own capital, but the numbers have grown too large for that, so they're now borrowing against the hardware itself. When infrastructure companies start leaning on leveraged loans to buy chips that depreciate fast, the financing risk of the AI boom stops being an equity story and becomes a credit one.

title: SEC Exempts Data-Center Bonds From Key Securitization Rules
blurb: The SEC exempted data-center bonds from key securitization rules, making it easier for owners to sell asset-backed securities. The move opens a wider debt channel for tech firms scrambling to fund the AI buildout, whose compute capex has outrun what cash flow and equity alone can cover. Expect more data-center ABS issuance ahead, which turns physical infrastructure into a financeable asset class and shifts some of the AI capital race onto the bond market, where the cost and pace of borrowing start to shape who can keep building.

title: Can Agents Use a Computer Yet? We've Got the Data
blurb: Computer-using agents have crossed from demo to production, holding up on narrow, repeatable back-office work like updating systems of record, moving data through portals, and processing tickets where no clean API exists. They still break when the work drifts off the runbook, and for cases where caching is intractable the cost math doesn't yet close. But the frontier is Business Process Outsourcing, and the structural edge is hard to argue with: an agent that works 24/7 and scales to demand is starting to beat humans clicking through legacy systems by hand.

title: Tel Aviv- and San Francisco-based Corma, which develops AI models for defensive cybersecurity, emerges from stealth with a $60M seed led by Sequoia Capital (Emily Forlini/Fortune)
blurb: Corma emerged from stealth with a $60M seed led by Sequoia Capital, one of the largest seed rounds in cybersecurity. The Tel Aviv- and San Francisco-based startup builds AI models aimed at defense rather than offense, betting that the same model capabilities powering automated attacks can be turned toward detecting and blocking them. The round size signals where security spend is heading, as investors position for a market in which AI-driven threats and AI-driven defenses escalate against each other.

title: Intel announces a $15B common stock offering, with proceeds going to general corporate purposes, like "maintaining a strong balance sheet"; INTC falls 3%+ (Ian King/Bloomberg)
blurb: Intel announced a $15B common stock offering, with proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes and, in its own words, "maintaining a strong balance sheet." Diluting shareholders to fund vague corporate purposes is what a company does when it needs cash and hasn't committed to where it goes, and the market read it that way, sending INTC down more than 3% on the news. For a company mid-turnaround on foundry and facing a capex bill it can't easily cover from operations, raising equity here signals the balance sheet is tighter than the strategy narrative suggests.

title: Global New Unicorn Counts In The First Half Of 2026 Have Already Surpassed 2025’s Totals
blurb: 195 companies joined the Crunchbase Unicorn Board in the first half of 2026, already topping the 193 minted in all of 2025 and the highest pace since late 2022. Robotics and AI neolabs led the cohort, with the US minting 110 of the new unicorns and China surging to 38, up from 10 a year earlier. The new class added roughly $440B in value on $80B raised, headlined by DeepSeek at $50B, and 19 of them doubled their valuation in fast follow-on rounds inside six months.

title: The Biggest Consequence Of An AI IPO Isn’t The IPO Itself. It’s What Happens Afterward.
blurb: The real story of the coming AI IPOs isn't how OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks, or Stripe trade after the bell. It's the distributions that hit limited partners once those exits clear, returning capital that venture has been starved of for years and freeing endowments, pension funds, and sovereign wealth to recommit. That liquidity is likely to concentrate rather than spread: the 10 largest US venture funds took nearly a third of all capital raised in 2025, while first-time fund formation fell to its lowest in over a decade. A sustained wave of listings won't lift the whole ecosystem evenly. It will hand the biggest managers the largest share.

title: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
blurb: TSMC's July revenue hit $14.5B, up 44.7% year on year, putting the world's biggest chipmaker ahead of its own guidance for 40% growth this year. High-performance computing, where TSMC books AI chip sales, now accounts for 66% of revenue, and the company raised 2026 capex to between $60B and $64B. TSMC builds for Nvidia and Google, so its monthly numbers are the cleanest read on whether Big Tech's AI infrastructure spend is still translating into real orders, and for now the answer is yes.

title: Whatnot raises $545M from ICONIQ, Lightspeed and Avra to fuel live commerce expansion
blurb: Whatnot raised $545M in a Series G at a $20B valuation, nearly doubling its worth in under a year, led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed, and Avra. In a year when venture capital has narrowed almost entirely to AI, a live-streaming marketplace for Funko Pops, Pokémon cards, and sneakers pulled in over half a billion dollars, with gross merchandise volume already topping last year's full total halfway through 2026. The global live commerce market is projected to hit $230B in 2026 and grow toward $2.55T by 2033, with Europe and North America the fastest-growing regions Whatnot is now targeting.

title: How Mailchimp Went From $1B+ ARR to … Shrinking Inside Intuit. A Death Spiral in the Age of AI?
blurb: Intuit paid roughly $12B for Mailchimp in 2021, and five years later it is publishing its growth rate with the asset stripped out. On its May 2026 call, Intuit's Online Ecosystem grew 19%, or 22% without Mailchimp, and management confirmed the unit's revenue is now declining while announcing a 17% workforce cut and about $300M in restructuring charges. The decline started before AI, but the agent era made it fatal: the entry point for new email moved from a marketer signing up for a UI to a developer or model provisioning it by API, and Mailchimp is not in that room.

title: Sila lands $1.4B Pentagon loan as militaries demand more batteries
blurb: The Pentagon just handed Sila a $1.4B loan to scale silicon-carbon battery material, part of a broader push to buy anode supply that doesn't run through China. Graphite anodes dominate today's lithium-ion cells and their supply chain is Chinese-controlled, so Sila's Moses Lake factory is one of the few tariff-free sources, with silicon promising 20% to 40% more energy density. The signal for founders: defense capital is now flowing into the unglamorous materials layer, and government loans plus contracts with Mercedes and Panasonic are becoming a viable path to scale hard-tech manufacturing.

title: The Deluge of AI Debt Has Big Names Seeking New Strategies to Avoid Selloffs
blurb: The AI buildout is now being funded with a wave of debt, and the biggest arrangers are engineering the deals specifically to keep fast-money investors from triggering a selloff. BlackRock structured its Meta data-center financing to lock in patient capital rather than let hedge funds churn the paper. The signal for founders is that the capital behind the AI infrastructure race is getting more fragile and more actively managed, which means the terms, not just the demand, will decide how long the spending holds up.

title: Sources: AI cloud computing provider Lambda is selling a $917M leveraged loan to finance the purchase of GPUs as part of a contract with Nvidia (Bloomberg)
blurb: Lambda is raising a $917M leveraged loan to buy the GPUs it needs for a new contract with Nvidia, according to Bloomberg. The structure is notable: an AI cloud provider borrowing against hardware that a chipmaker is both supplying and, through these deals, effectively backstopping demand for. It is another sign that the capital fueling the AI buildout increasingly runs in circles among a handful of players, with debt against depreciating GPUs doing the heavy lifting.

title: Unitree’s Shanghai IPO 5,526 Times Subscribed by Retail Buyers
blurb: Unitree's Shanghai IPO was oversubscribed 5,526 times by retail investors, one of the frothiest debuts China has seen for a hardware maker. The demand signals that public markets now treat humanoid robotics the way they treated EVs and solar a decade ago, betting on a category before the unit economics are proven. For founders in physical AI, the read is that capital is racing ahead of revenue, and the winners will be the ones who can convert that enthusiasm into shipped units before the subsidy-and-hype cycle turns.

title: Sources: officials say OpenAI risks its White House relationship by hiring Dean Ball, who has criticized Trump's AI strategy after leaving the administration (Thomas Barrabi/New York Post)
blurb: OpenAI risks its White House relationship by hiring Dean Ball, a former administration official who has publicly criticized Trump's AI strategy since leaving. The move is a bet that the policy expertise Ball brings is worth more than the political goodwill it costs, at a moment when frontier labs are lobbying hard over federal AI rules. For founders, it is a reminder that in AI, regulatory access is now a competitive asset, and even the largest players are willing to spend relationships to shape the rules they will operate under.

title: GameStop May Pull $56 Billion EBay Bid
blurb: GameStop may pull its $56B bid for eBay and pitch a partnership instead, according to people familiar with the matter. CEO Ryan Cohen appears to be backing away from a full acquisition toward a lighter structural tie-up. The retreat signals how hard it is to finance a deal of that size in the current market, and it leaves eBay's strategic direction unresolved just as Cohen's ambitions to reshape GameStop into a broader retail and investment vehicle come under closer scrutiny.

title: Intel Shares Fall After Announcing $15 Billion Stock Offering
blurb: Intel is selling $15B in common stock to fund an AI push, and shares fell on the news. The dilution signals how far behind Intel is in AI: it needs to raise fresh equity to chase opportunities that Nvidia, AMD, and the hyperscalers are already funding from cash flow. Investors read a $15B raise from a company with Intel's balance sheet as a sign the catch-up bill is large and the return is uncertain.

title: JPMorgan Leads $441 Million Debt Deal for AI Infrastructure Firm
blurb: Global AI, a two-year-old startup, raised $441M in debt financing led by JPMorgan to build out AI data centers. Debt, not equity, is increasingly how infrastructure firms fund the capital-heavy buildout, because banks will lend against contracted capacity and hardware they can collateralize without diluting founders. The signal for operators is that the money chasing AI is splitting in two, with venture funding the software layer and project finance underwriting the physical layer, and a two-year-old company clearing a nine-figure debt deal shows how fast that second track has matured.

title: Q&A with Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour on his vision to "financialize everything", sports betting, Kalshi's "philosophical misalignment" with Polymarket, and more (Jordyn Holman/New York Times)
blurb: Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour wants to turn nearly any real-world question into a tradable market, from sports outcomes to elections to economic events. He frames the company's split with Polymarket as philosophical, positioning Kalshi as the regulated, CFTC-compliant venue rather than a crypto-native one. The bet is that prediction markets stop being a novelty and become a mainstream asset class, and the founders watching this should note that a fully regulated on-ramp is what turns a fringe product into infrastructure everyone else has to build around.

title: SpaceX stock rebounds to near $135 IPO price
blurb: SpaceX shares climbed back near their $135 IPO price on Monday, recovering from a post-debut slump that closed as low as $108.27 days earlier. The rebound follows a first earnings report that beat expectations at $7.81B in Q2 revenue, with the CFO guiding to $100B in annualized recurring revenue by year-end on the back of its neocloud business and Cursor acquisition. The swings came as a 911 million-share lockup expired and short interest topped Tesla's, but most analysts stayed bullish, with Citi reiterating a buy and a $200 target.

title: Whatnot Closes $545M Series G at $20B Valuation
blurb: Whatnot raised $545M in a Series G at a $20B valuation, nearly double the $11.5B it hit in its Series F just ten months earlier. The livestream shopping marketplace has already passed its full-year 2025 GMV halfway through 2026, more than doubled its buyer base, and now adds over 650,000 people a week. Live commerce, long treated as a China-only phenomenon, is compounding fast enough in the US that one in eight Whatnot sellers now runs a full-time business on the platform.

title: Workers Say AI Took Over Colleagues' Tasks as Jobs Data Shows No Measurable Shift
blurb: One in five employed US adults now say AI handles at least one task their team used to hand off to a coworker or contractor, according to a July Epoch AI and Ipsos survey. That substitution is happening inside jobs that still exist, because the Yale Budget Lab found no detectable change in employment or inflation-adjusted wages across AI-exposed occupations as of May 2026. Weekly AI use remains a minority habit, concentrated among workers earning $100,000 or more, so the tooling is redistributing work inside companies faster than it is showing up in payrolls.

title: UK AI funding skyrocketed in first half of the year
blurb: UK AI companies raised $9.6bn in the first half of 2026, up 360% from the same period last year, even as deal count fell to 69 rounds from 74. The money is pooling at the top, with the five most-funded firms taking 84% of the total and Isomorphic Labs, Nscale, and Wayve alone pulling in $5.3bn. London captured 98% of it, leaving Oxford a distant second at $103m, so the UK's AI capital is now a single-city game with fewer, much larger checks.

title: UK air defence company Cambridge Aerospace raises €259.7 million Series C at €2.94 billion valuation
blurb: Cambridge Aerospace raised €259.7M ($300M) at a €2.94B valuation, roughly tripling its worth in the four months since its April Series B. The UK company builds low-cost interceptor missiles for European and allied militaries, and its first product, Skyhammer, is already under contract with the UK Ministry of Defence. Founded less than two years ago by an ex-MIT professor and an Anduril veteran, it now employs more than 250 people across six countries, a sign of how fast European defence tech is compounding as governments race to rearm.

title: Discovered Materials is playing AI whack-a-mole to hunt cooler chips
blurb: Discovered Materials raised a $9M seed to run swarms of AI agents hunting cooler semiconductor materials, doing thousands of candidate guesses a day.

title: OpenAI kauft NextSlide: Dieses neue Tool könnte jetzt für ChatGPT kommen
blurb: OpenAI acquired NextSlide, a year-old San Francisco startup whose AI turned prompts, notes, and documents into editable presentations, and folded the team into ChatGPT development. The deal closed quietly earlier this year and only surfaced when founder Ahmed Beshry posted about it, with no price disclosed. The pattern is familiar: frontier labs are absorbing single-feature startups to build slide generation, coding, and other workflows directly into the assistant, leaving thin wrappers on ChatGPT with less room to stand alone.

title: UK AI funding rockets 360% to £7.2bn
blurb: UK AI companies raised $9.6bn in H1 2026, up 360% from a year earlier, even though the number of rounds held flat at 69. The money is concentrating hard: the top five companies took 84% of the total, with Isomorphic Labs, Nscale, and Wayve alone pulling in $5.3bn, and London captured 98% of all UK AI funding. AI infrastructure led every sector at $5.4bn, so the surge is less a broad-based boom than a handful of large, capital-intensive bets on compute and foundation models.

title: Aurrigo awarded £1.43m grant for autonomous airport vehicles
blurb: Aurrigo won a £1.43m UK government grant under the CAM Pathfinder scheme to test whether autonomous vehicles can handle airside safety work, from perimeter patrols to chasing birds off runways. The company already runs autonomous luggage and cargo platforms across eight international airports, so the new SENTRY project pushes driverless tech from moving bags to inspecting the dark, hazardous zones staff currently walk on foot. Trials run at Teesside and Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky with the CAA setting the rules, a sign that airside autonomy is moving from cargo novelty toward regulated safety operations.

title: Edgify raises $9M from Rank Ventures and Mangrove Capital to bring AI to supermarket shelves and checkouts
blurb: Edgify raised $9M from Rank Ventures and Mangrove Capital, taking total funding to $25M, to run AI directly on the cameras, scales, and checkouts a store already owns. Each device trains locally and shares what it learns across the network, so a scan-avoidance trick caught at one till spreads to the rest without any footage leaving the building. The interesting part isn't the grocery use case but the direction of travel: AI spend is moving from the cloud toward the physical infrastructure that already sits on-site, with the edge AI market projected to grow from about $47B in 2026 to $446B by 2034.

title: Meta Muse Glimmer – open weights 30B local coding model
blurb: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter agentic model under Apache 2.0 that runs locally on a single consumer GPU for coding, function calling, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation. Trained by distilling agentic reasoning from the larger Muse Spark teacher, it ships with open weights on Hugging Face and gets llama.cpp, MLX, and ExecuTorch integrations in the coming days.

title: Meta returns to open source with Muse Glimmer, an Apache 2.0 licensed 30B parameter AI model optimized for agents — available now
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter dense open-weight model under Apache 2.0, its first fully open release since dropping the Llama family for the proprietary Muse Spark in April. The weights are on Hugging Face now, with Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and llama.cpp support rolling out this week, and the permissive license drops Llama's 700M-monthly-user cap for unrestricted commercial use.

title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer for local AI agents
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0 built for always-on local agents running on a single consumer GPU across Mac or PC. Quantization drops the language model under 20 GB to fit a 24 GB or 32 GB envelope, and a DFlash speculative-decoding drafter reports decode-speed gains of 3.1x on an RTX 5090 and 1.8x on an M5 Max.

title: Tail-call optimization in C is relatively recent
blurb: This LWN comment explains why C compilers lacked tail-call optimization for decades: the C calling convention makes the caller, not the callee, clean up stack arguments, so a call followed by a return could not collapse into a jump. GCC and Clang now handle these tail calls (including the interpreter-dispatch pattern), which lets Copy-and-Patch style interpreters scale to 100,000 code snippets rather than the sub-2,000 practical under goto-based dispatch.

title: Python Now Has a Post-Quantum Encryption Library
blurb: pyca/cryptography now ships support for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, the NIST-standard post-quantum key-establishment and digital-signature primitives, making post-quantum crypto a single pip install for the Python ecosystem. The work was funded by the Sovereign Tech Agency, and the case for adopting it now is crypto agility rather than urgency, since no quantum threat is imminent.

title: What a Claude Code subagent actually costs: measuring the ~436k-token fixed overhead
blurb: The author measured Claude Code subagent costs from session JSONL transcripts and found each spawned subagent carries roughly 436k tokens of fixed overhead, from initial context load plus the final-turn cache write, versus only about 46k tokens for the embedded content it actually reviews.
