The post shows how to reproduce the measurement and concludes that agent headcount, not payload size, is the real cost lever, making full-content embedding nearly free by comparison.

title: Animating CSS border-image
blurb: Andy Clarke revisited CSS border-image, and this post extends it to animated border images and gradients, noting they can't curve to rounded corners.

title: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
blurb: Meta released Muse Glimmer, an open-source dense 30B multimodal model that pairs a 2B Perception Encoder for vision with a 28B text decoder, with day-0 support in transformers, llama.cpp, and vLLM. The decoder uses hybrid attention alternating three 2,048-token sliding-window layers with a full-attention NoPE layer, plus gated grouped-query attention that shares each KV head across 16 query heads to cut KV-cache memory 16x.

title: Claude Code puts auto mode in the driver's seat
blurb: The author examines Claude Code's auto mode, which lets the agent plan and execute multi-step coding tasks without pausing for approval at each step. The piece weighs the productivity gain against the loss of human checkpoints, noting that autonomous agents still ship incomplete fixes and regressions when left to run unsupervised, so the reviewer's job shifts from writing code to auditing what the agent already merged.

title: Controlling a treadmill from an iPhone over Bluetooth LE
blurb: The author built Treadmill Pro, a SwiftUI iOS app that drives a treadmill's speed, incline, and live stats directly over Bluetooth Low Energy with CoreBluetooth, bypassing the vendor's companion app. The post explains the FTMS fitness-machine profile, the connect-discover-subscribe-write lifecycle, and why a BLE controller is really a state machine that must handle a take-control handshake, exact byte decoding, and devices that vanish mid-run.

title: I got tired of heavyweight Markdown editors, so I built one in Rust + Tauri that doesn't ship a browser
blurb: Bokuchi is an open-source Markdown editor built with Tauri v2, Rust, and React that renders through the OS-native WebView instead of bundling a Chromium instance like Electron apps do. The result is a small footprint and near-instant startup, with the trade-off being reliance on platform WebViews (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK) whose rendering behavior varies across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: Introducing FILE type: a native column type for multimodal data
blurb: Databricks announced the beta of FILE, a new column type that stores unstructured data like documents, images, and video as a native, governed column alongside structured tables. Databricks is building the format into open Parquet and Delta Lake, so multimodal data stays queryable and secured in the lakehouse without living in a separate system or locking teams to one vendor.

title: Microsoft’s PostgreSQL alternative, HorizonDB: Worth the wait?
blurb: Microsoft's HorizonDB, the cloud-native PostgreSQL alternative it pitched at Ignite in November 2025, remains in public preview nine months later with no announced GA date, even as AWS Aurora, Google AlloyDB, Databricks Lakebase, and Snowflake Postgres ship production-ready PostgreSQL services for the same AI workloads. Analysts say the undefined GA date, pricing, and SLAs give enterprises with urgent AI projects little reason to wait, though Azure-committed shops readying Foundry and Fabric integrations may still hold out.

title: Metabase Patches Vulnerability Exploited as Zero-Day
blurb: Metabase released urgent patches for a critical SQL injection vulnerability that was exploited in the wild as a zero-day against Metabase Cloud, letting remote, unauthenticated attackers inject arbitrary queries and gain admin access to stored database credentials and any connected data. Metabase Cloud instances are already patched, but self-hosted users on versions 63.5, 62.9, 61.11, 60.17, 59.21, and 58.24 should apply the fix immediately and rotate credentials for all connected databases.

title: dbt Semantic Layer vs Cube vs AtScale: Choosing an Enterprise Semantic Layer
blurb: The author compares dbt Semantic Layer, Cube, and AtScale and argues all three define metrics well but none answers whether an AI agent is entitled to run one. The shared gaps are that coverage stops at whatever someone modeled, so unmodeled intent has no answer, and entitlements get filtered around the query rather than inside it, meaning data moves before authorization applies. The piece proposes evaluating on agent-facing tests like per-user SQL and reproducing a six-month-old number, not feature matrices.

title: Realistic AI architectural renderings must be labelled under EU AI Act
blurb: Realistic AI-generated architectural renderings published in the EU without a disclosure label now risk fines under Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which took effect on 2 August. The rule pulls architecture visualization studios into the same transparency regime as deepfakes, forcing anyone passing off synthetic imagery as real to mark it or face enforcement.

title: Animating CSS border-image
blurb: Andy Clarke's recent piece revisits CSS border-image to show it can carry gradients and sliced artwork instead of solid or dashed lines, and this tutorial pushes that further into animated borders that travel around a card. The author favors border-image over mask-based approaches for efficiency, since border-image-slice replicates a single gradient slice across all four edges automatically, with the caveat that it won't follow curved corners.

title: Satyress designs centaur-like robot to give workers "superpowers" for dangerous jobs
blurb: Satyress released Threehalves, a teleoperated centaur-like robot built to let workers handle dangerous jobs from a safe distance, with a wheeled quadruped base supporting a humanoid upper body. Founder Beau Gaston has developed the machine since 2022 and first shared it quietly on X, positioning it against the bipedal-humanoid race as a more stable platform for hazardous industrial work.

title: Bottle your judgment, Chat is the wrong UI, Design.md
blurb: Dan Maccarone argues that AI's next frontier for designers is not replacing judgment but productizing it, capturing the method one expert has spent a career building and handing that decision-making process to anyone. The roundup pairs this with pieces on why chat is the wrong interface for AI agents and how design systems increasingly let designers decide flow while tools resolve the visual details.

title: Python Now Has a Post-Quantum Encryption Library
blurb: pyca/cryptography added support for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, the NIST-standard post-quantum key-establishment and digital-signature primitives, making post-quantum crypto one pip install away for the Python ecosystem. The work was funded by the Sovereign Tech Agency, and adopting it now buys crypto agility ahead of any real quantum threat rather than during an emergency.

title: Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open in note taking app
blurb: A broken tenant-isolation flaw in AI meeting-recorder tl;dv exposes its entire Firestore `meetings` collection to any authenticated user, leaking over 181,000 recordings' creator emails, provider data, and live conference IDs across 2M+ accounts. Roughly 1,000 calls sit in `recording` status at any moment with joinable Google Meet and Teams IDs, letting an attacker walk into live sessions uninvited; the database has remained open six months after disclosure.

title: OpenAI Pauses Some Astra Work After Flagging Possible Critical Cyber Capabilities
blurb: OpenAI said Friday it cannot rule out that its unreleased Astra model has reached the Critical cyber threshold, meaning it could autonomously develop zero-day exploits or execute novel end-to-end attacks from a high-level goal, and paused internal activities that do not meet strengthened security controls. Astra would be OpenAI's first model to potentially qualify for Critical under its Preparedness Framework, above the High rating given to GPT-5.6-Sol and earlier models.

title: Kimsuky Builds Offline AI Stack to Boost Phishing and Automate Malware Development
blurb: Genians linked North Korea's Kimsuky group to offline AI infrastructure running Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty, including a configured GPT4All LocalDocs RAG database that connected the actor's own documents to a local model for phishing and malware-development tasks. With no vulnerability to patch, defenders should stop grading lures on polish and instead correlate LNK execution, PowerShell, hidden scheduled tasks, GitHub traffic, and downstream payload activity.

title: LexisNexis shuts down services after suspicious activity on servers
blurb: LexisNexis took its Nexis Diligence, Metabase API, and Newsdesk services offline after detecting unusual activity on servers hosted by an unnamed third-party vendor, and is rebuilding the affected systems in a new environment with help from a forensics firm. The company says the incident is unrelated to the recent Metabase Cloud SQL-injection zero-day, and follows a May 2025 GitHub breach that exposed data on 364,000 people.

title: CISA: SonicWall SMA1000 flaws now exploited by ransomware gangs
blurb: CISA added two patched SonicWall SMA1000 flaws (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, one a maximum-severity SSRF) to its KEV Catalog, confirming ransomware gangs are now exploiting them for VPN gateway access. Shadowserver tracks over 380 exposed appliances, and Volexity ties zero-day exploitation back to June 22 by UTA0533, so treat unpatched edge SMA1000 devices as already compromised.

title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA
blurb: Three research teams disclosed ways to defeat passkey protections without breaking their cryptography: SpecterOps reused signed authentication material to impersonate privileged Entra ID users while satisfying phishing-resistant MFA, Unit 42 recovered synced private keys from Google Password Manager in Chrome, and Dirk-jan Mollema abused a hardware-bound Windows Hello for Business key from a compromised session. Microsoft patched the related logging flaw CVE-2026-34348 (CVSS 6.5) and applied Entra-side mitigations for the relay-assertion issue.

title: New Jersey, Alabama Join States Targeted in Water Cyberattacks
blurb: Iran-linked hackers have targeted operational technology at water and wastewater utilities across at least 12 US states since late July, with New Jersey and Alabama the latest to confirm intrusions into ICS devices made by Rockwell Automation. Impact has been limited so far, with disruptions confined to phone systems and precautionary shutdowns rather than water service; CISA has urged the sector to secure exposed OT.

title: Metabase Patches Vulnerability Exploited as Zero-Day
blurb: Metabase released urgent patches for a critical SQL injection flaw (no CVE assigned) that lets remote, unauthenticated attackers inject arbitrary queries and gain administrative access, after a threat actor exploited it as a zero-day against Metabase Cloud. Self-hosted users should patch to versions 63.5, 62.9, 61.11, 60.17, 59.21, or 58.24, block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint where patching isn't possible, and rotate connected-database credentials.

title: North Korea’s Kimsuky integrates AI into cyberattacks targeting crypto and finance
blurb: North Korea's Kimsuky threat group is operating three local LLM environments built on Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty to develop malware, automate attacks, and generate polished phishing lures targeting crypto and fintech firms, according to Genians. The offline, RAG-capable setups keep queries off external cloud services, and defenders should treat crypto-themed lures imitating Korean investment platforms as likely Kimsuky-authored given the group stole $2.02B in cryptocurrency last year.

title: OpenAI’s Upcoming Astra Model Raises Autonomous Cyberattack Concerns
blurb: OpenAI flagged its unreleased Astra model as potentially the first to hit the "critical" cybersecurity tier of its Preparedness Framework, the threshold for autonomously building zero-days against hardened systems and running end-to-end attacks from a high-level goal. The company suspended internal Astra projects lacking mandated controls, deploying isolated testing, network restrictions, weight protections, and chain-of-thought monitors that intercept high-risk behavior ahead of government and third-party red-teaming.

title: Valve notifies Steam hardware customers of a data breach
blurb: Valve is notifying European Steam hardware customers that attackers breached its shipping partner CEVA Logistics between July 29 and August 1, 2026, exfiltrating names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and ordered product details. No payment data, passwords, or Steam Guard codes were exposed, but the stolen delivery information enables convincing phishing that impersonates Steam or couriers and cites victims' real addresses to establish legitimacy.

title: Crypto exchange Coinsbuy loses $8 million in coordinated two-blockchain attack
blurb: An attacker drained $8.07 million from crypto exchange Coinsbuy across TRON and Ethereum in under an hour on Aug. 9, with onchain researchers linking both chains into a single operation through cross-chain swapper Bridgers. Roughly 79% of the funds moved through instant exchange FixedFloat across 50 single-use addresses; Coinsbuy refilled the drained wallets within 24 hours and says the attack vector remains unestablished.

title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
blurb: Security researcher Cory Solovewicz bought the placeholder domains noreply.net and noreply.us and set them as catch-alls, turning them into an accidental honeypot that has logged 401,796 misdirected emails since December 2024. Organizations misconfigure internal systems to send injury reports, test-platform credentials, and account-setup messages to these @noreply addresses, so defenders should audit any placeholder or no-reply domains their systems mail to and confirm they resolve internally.

title: Cisco Warns of High-Severity ClamAV Vulnerabilities With Public PoC
blurb: Cisco warned that its Secure Endpoint Connector products on Windows, macOS, and Linux are affected by seven ClamAV parser flaws (CVE-2026-20337 through CVE-2026-20339 and CVE-2026-20345 through CVE-2026-20348) that enable denial-of-service, with public PoC code for two. No workaround exists and the ClamAV process runs privileged on Windows, so admins should push the 1.5.4-based fixes shipping in August Connector releases.

title: Framework loses customer data in Metabase zero-day attack
blurb: Framework disclosed that attackers exploited a zero-day in its self-hosted Metabase analytics instance to exfiltrate customer data, including names, email addresses, and shipping details tied to orders. Organizations running internet-exposed Metabase should treat the deployment as a breach vector, restrict it behind authenticated access, and monitor for unauthorized queries against connected production databases while awaiting or applying the vendor patch.

title: ‘Ghostjacking’ Attack Uses Poisoned Logs to Turn AI Agents Bad
blurb: Tenet researchers demonstrated Ghostjacking at DEF CON, an attack that plants malicious instructions as plain text in logs and alerts on Cloudflare, Datadog, and Sentry, so an AI agent asked to review the event reads and executes them. One vector abuses Cloudflare's managed firewall rule, which logs blocked requests verbatim and hijacked DNS 9 out of 10 times against Claude Code; scope filtered agent tool permissions and treat log content as untrusted input.

title: N-able ships second N-central hotfix as attackers keep exploiting CVE-2026-18577
blurb: N-able released a second N-central hotfix (version 2026.3.1.10) for CVE-2026-18577, an authentication-bypass that patches a variation of the earlier CVE-2026-18556 and has been exploited in the wild since August 1. Post-exploitation, the threat actor abuses N-central's legitimate Take Control feature to reach managed endpoints, registers a Cloudflare tunnel service for persistence, and creates a "veeam" domain account while resetting existing domain admin passwords.

title: Cyber vulnerability sweep picks up Royal Navy drones sending data to China
blurb: A UK government cyber vulnerability sweep found that drones operated by the Royal Navy were transmitting data to servers in China, according to The Register. The exposure points to a supply-chain problem in the drone hardware or firmware rather than a discrete CVE, so defenders running similar commercial UAV fleets should audit outbound telemetry destinations and network-isolate the devices pending vendor review.

title: OpenAI tightens controls on its new model over cybersecurity risks, as AI security debate intensifies
blurb: OpenAI halted some internal activities involving its unreleased Astra model after preliminary evaluations indicated it could reach "Critical" capability, meaning autonomous cyberattacks against hardened defenses without step-by-step prompting. The disclosure follows recent incidents involving Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta models and adds momentum to the "AI Kill Switch Act," which would require labs to retain the ability to shut down, throttle, or suspend their models.

title: UK's Royal Navy sea drones contain component that secretly sent data to China, report claims — government cuts camera connectivity and insists data wasn’t sensitive, only ‘heartbeat communications’
blurb: K3 Scout sea drones used by the UK's Royal Navy carried a Chinese camera component that covertly transmitted data to China, per a Telegraph report, with the flaw surfacing during a routine cyber vulnerability assessment. The MoD has cut all internet connectivity from the cameras and characterizes the traffic as low-scope "heartbeat communications," though sources cite concerns the drones could have snooped on sensitive special forces meetings even when powered off.

title: TrueConf Server Flaws Exploited to Replace Client Installers with PhantomCore
blurb: Head Mare is chaining two TrueConf videoconferencing server flaws (KLCERT-26-057 and KLCERT-26-058) to gain NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM code execution, then replacing the legitimate TrueConf client installer with a poisoned build that drops the PhantomCore backdoor at Russian industrial, energy, and IT firms. The bugs affect TrueConf server versions through 5.3.9, 5.4.9, and 5.5.5, and are reachable via the default-open TCP port 4307, so patch and restrict that port immediately.

title: A data breach at shipping giant Ceva Logistics is rippling across banks, retailers, Steam gamers, and beyond
blurb: A breach at logistics giant Ceva Logistics, which began July 29, exposed the names, home addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of downstream retail customers whose orders it fulfills, hitting ING, Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ajax, Ace & Tate, and Valve's Steam hardware buyers. The attack also disrupted at least eight European warehouses, and organizations relying on Ceva for fulfillment should notify affected customers and watch for phishing that leverages the stolen shipping data.

title: Member of The Com sent to prison for blackmail, sextortion
blurb: Justin Swaddle, a 20-year-old Leeds man and member of the cybercrime collective The Com, was sentenced to two years in prison after pleading guilty to blackmail and child sexual abuse offenses tied to sextortion of 117 female victims aged 13 to 17 worldwide. The NCA identified the victims after taking over the case in January 2024, recovering device evidence of coerced self-harm and category A to C indecent imagery.

title: You Don’t Need to Hack a Company. Sometimes They’ll Email You Their Secrets.
blurb: Security researcher Cory Solovewicz bought noreply.net and noreply.us and received over 400,000 misdirected emails from roughly 6,200 root domains, including test credentials, employee and customer data, injury reports, and more than 28,000 attachments. The lesson for defenders is that "noreply" and deleted-user addresses are not dead ends. Any external domain your automated systems email can be registered and configured as a catch-all, so audit outbound mail destinations and keep sending domains you control from lapsing.

title: Attackers pick Levi's pockets in social engineering attack
blurb: Attackers compromised Levi Strauss through a social engineering campaign, gaining access to internal systems by manipulating employees rather than exploiting a technical vulnerability. Social engineering remains the dominant initial-access vector for retail breaches, so defenders should prioritize phishing-resistant MFA, help-desk identity verification for password and MFA resets, and out-of-band confirmation before granting any employee-requested account changes.

title: Signed up for Klaviyo? Dozens of advertisers may have seen your password
blurb: Klaviyo left its sign-up web form misconfigured from at least February 2024 through November 2025, leaking new customers' email addresses and plaintext passwords to embedded third-party trackers from Facebook, Google, HubSpot, Microsoft, LinkedIn, and X. Klaviyo has fixed the pixel-related configuration bug and says fewer than 2,000 individuals were affected, but customers who signed up in that window should rotate their Klaviyo passwords and any credentials reused elsewhere.

title: Tel Aviv- and San Francisco-based Corma, which develops AI models for defensive cybersecurity, emerges from stealth with a $60M seed led by Sequoia Capital (Emily Forlini/Fortune)
blurb: Corma emerged from stealth with a $60M seed round led by Sequoia Capital to build AI models for defensive cybersecurity. The company, based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, joins a growing field of startups applying frontier models to detection, triage, and automated response as defenders look to counter AI-accelerated attacks.

title: Steam hardware shipper breach leaks customer data, including names and addresses
blurb: Valve disclosed that its European shipping partner CEVA Logistics suffered a breach between July 29 and August 1, exposing names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of customers who reserved Steam Machine and Steam Controller hardware. CEVA held no payment data, passwords, or Steam Guard codes, but Valve warns of phishing that quotes victims' real addresses to request fake delivery or customs fees.

title: Stealthium Targets Security Blind Spots in AI Accelerators and Neo-Clouds
blurb: Stealthium launched a security tool that detects compromise of AI accelerators and neo-clouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, where traditional CPU-centric tooling has no visibility into high-speed accelerator video memory. Because Stealthium cannot see inside the accelerators directly, it runs an agent in the customer's own infrastructure trained to spot subtle signals of a compromised neo-cloud, addressing a supply-chain blind spot the recent Januscape malware could have exploited.

title: Cyberattack on Steam hardware shipper leaks names, addresses, and order data
blurb: Valve is notifying European Steam customers of a data breach at CEVA Logistics, its hardware shipping partner, where an attacker active between July 29 and August 1 likely stole names, street addresses, phone numbers, account email addresses, and ordered-hardware details. No payment data, passwords, or Steam Guard codes were exposed, but the leaked delivery details enable convincing order-themed phishing, so treat any message quoting your address or requesting a customs or redelivery fee as fraudulent.

title: Data of European Steam hardware customers 'likely compromised', Valve says
blurb: Valve disclosed that European customers who purchased Steam hardware likely had some personal data compromised, though the company has not detailed the exposure scope or attack vector. Affected customers should watch for targeted phishing referencing their hardware orders and treat any account-recovery or shipping-update messages tied to the purchase as suspect until Valve confirms what data was accessed.

title: Microsoft Entra ID is removing an extra MFA hurdle for Windows Hello and macOS PSSO users
blurb: Microsoft Entra ID will stop requiring WHfB and macOS PSSO users to register an extra passkey for MFA, rolling out worldwide from early October 2026.

title: Valve informs customers about data breach, personal data stolen
blurb: Valve notified customers that a third-party vendor handling Steam hardware deliveries was breached, exposing personal data tied to those shipments. Affected customers should treat delivery-related details such as names, addresses, and contact information as compromised and stay alert for phishing or social-engineering attempts referencing recent Steam hardware orders.

title: Microsoft Entra ID has a big change coming for Windows Hello for Business and macOS PSSO
blurb: Microsoft is updating Entra ID to let Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO function as standalone MFA factors, rather than requiring a separate second factor after passwordless sign-in. The change lets phishing-resistant device credentials satisfy MFA policies on their own, simplifying Conditional Access design for endpoints that already enroll hardware-bound keys. Microsoft plans to begin the rollout later this year.

title: Steam hardware distributor hit by cyberattack, 'expect fake messages,' Valve warns — Europe vendor has personal information and hardware purchase details stolen
blurb: Steam's European hardware distributor CEVA Logistics was breached between July 29 and August 1, 2026, exposing names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and order details for Steam Deck and Steam Machine buyers from the prior 90 days. Payment data, passwords, and Steam Guard codes were not taken, but Valve warns affected customers to expect targeted phishing via email, SMS, and phone impersonating Steam or delivery firms and demanding bogus customs or delivery fees.

title: Trust your AI agents? New research shows ‘memory poisoning’ can dupe them into ‘remembering’ fake information – and it’s a huge security risk
blurb: Forcepoint researchers disclosed "memory poisoning," an indirect prompt-injection variant that plants fake vendors, support contacts, or security rules into an AI agent's persistent memory layer, where the agent later retrieves and trusts them as fact across sessions. Unlike session-bound prompt injection, poisoned items delivered via web pages, shared documents, support tickets, or hidden PDF text persist and can steer harmful decisions months later.

title: CISA: SonicWall SMA1000 flaws now exploited by ransomware gangs
blurb: CISA added two recently patched SonicWall SMA1000 flaws, including a maximum-severity SSRF bug (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and now flags both as targeted by ransomware gangs. Enterprises, government agencies, and MSSPs running the remote-access gateway should apply SonicWall's July hotfix immediately, as Shadowserver still tracks over 380 exposed appliances and threat actors have exploited the bugs since June 22.

title: LexisNexis shuts down services after suspicious activity on servers
blurb: LexisNexis took its Nexis Diligence, Metabase API, and Newsdesk services offline after detecting unusual activity on servers run by an unnamed third-party vendor, and is now rebuilding the affected systems in a new environment with help from a forensic firm. The outage cuts off due-diligence, media-monitoring, and data-feed tools that compliance, PR, and enterprise integration teams rely on, marking the third security incident to hit the data-analytics provider since March 2025.

title: Valve notifies Steam hardware customers of a data breach
blurb: Valve began notifying European Steam hardware customers that attackers stole their delivery data after breaching its shipping partner CEVA Logistics, exposing names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and order details between July 29 and August 1. No payment data, passwords, or Steam Guard codes were compromised, but the third-party breach exposes the supply-chain risk in outsourced logistics and sets up a wave of targeted phishing against affected buyers.

title: New Passkey Attacks Can Recover Synced Private Keys or Bypass Phishing-Resistant MFA
blurb: Researchers at SpecterOps, Unit 42, and Dirk-jan Mollema demonstrated three separate ways to defeat passkey protections without breaking their cryptography, including recovering private keys for Google Password Manager synced passkeys and impersonating privileged Entra ID users while satisfying phishing-resistant MFA. Microsoft patched the related Windows logging flaw (CVE-2026-34348, CVSS 6.5) and applied Entra-side mitigations, but its own migration guidance still describes passkeys as replay-resistant.

title: New Jersey, Alabama Join States Targeted in Water Cyberattacks
blurb: At least 12 US states have now reported cyberattacks on their water and wastewater facilities since late July, with New Jersey and Alabama the latest to confirm intrusions into OT and industrial control systems tied to Iranian hackers targeting Rockwell Automation devices. Impact has been limited so far, but CISA is urging the water sector to harden OT, and New York has committed over $9M in grants to shore up utility cybersecurity.

title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
blurb: A security researcher who owns the placeholder domains noreply.net and noreply.us has received roughly 700 misdirected emails per day, more than 400,000 since December 2024, containing injury reports, account credentials, and other sensitive data companies assumed were going nowhere. Presented at Defcon, the finding is a reminder that internal systems routing mail to noreply-style domains can leak confidential information to whoever happens to own them.

title: Framework loses customer data in Metabase zero-day attack
blurb: Framework disclosed that attackers exploited a zero-day in Metabase, the open-source business intelligence tool, to access a database containing customer names, email addresses, and shipping details. The breach adds Metabase to the growing list of self-hosted analytics and BI platforms drawing active exploitation, pushing IT teams to audit internet-facing deployments and confirm that patch timelines keep pace with vendor advisories.

title: Cisco Warns of High-Severity ClamAV Vulnerabilities With Public PoC
blurb: Cisco warned that its Secure Endpoint Connector products on Windows, macOS, and Linux are affected by seven high-severity ClamAV parsing vulnerabilities that can trigger denial-of-service conditions, with public proof-of-concept code already circulating for two of them. No workaround exists, and patched Secure Endpoint Connector releases roll out in August, leaving Windows deployments most exposed because they run the ClamAV scanner in a privileged context.

title: ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE: Balancing control and autonomy for your microservices
blurb: Google added ClusterNetworkPolicy (CNP) to GKE, a cluster-wide, non-bypassable network security resource from the Kubernetes SIG-Policy Working Group that uses a tiered admin/namespace/baseline hierarchy to resolve the policy conflicts that plague standard namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy. Platform and security teams can now enforce compliance mandates and a default deny-all zero-trust posture centrally via RBAC, while developers still write their own application policies without overriding the guardrails.

title: N-able ships second N-central hotfix as attackers keep exploiting CVE-2026-18577
blurb: N-able released a second N-central hotfix (version 2026.3.1.10) after attackers kept exploiting CVE-2026-18577, an authentication bypass that evades the patch shipped in Hotfix 1 earlier this month. MSPs running self-hosted N-central must apply Hotfix 2 immediately, since threat actors are chaining the bypass with the legitimate Take Control feature to reach managed endpoints and plant CloudFlare tunnels for persistence.

title: Microsoft Entra ID is removing an extra MFA hurdle for Windows Hello and macOS PSSO users
blurb: Microsoft Entra ID will let Windows Hello for Business and macOS PSSO satisfy MFA without registering a second passkey, rolling out October through November 2026.

title: Cyber vulnerability sweep picks up Royal Navy drones sending data to China
blurb: A UK government cyber vulnerability sweep found that drones operated by the Royal Navy were transmitting data to servers in China, exposing a supply-chain risk in fielded hardware. The finding pushes defense and enterprise buyers to audit the firmware and network behavior of imported IoT and edge devices, since vendor-level data exfiltration can pass procurement checks that only vet the hardware.

title: As datacenters expand, so does public opposition to them
blurb: Public opposition to datacenter construction is mounting as communities push back against the water, power, and land demands of hyperscale buildouts, with local governments increasingly blocking or delaying new projects. For IT leaders planning capacity, the growing permitting friction adds siting risk and lead-time uncertainty to expansion roadmaps, strengthening the case for existing colocation and regional cloud regions over greenfield facilities.

title: Serving the most critical missions: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status
blurb: Cloudflare for Government achieved FedRAMP High authorization, sponsored by NIST and up from the Moderate authorization it held since 2022. The company is now building on those controls to pursue U.S. Department of Defense Impact Level 4 authorization, positioning its global network to serve federal agencies and defense contractors handling controlled unclassified data alongside AWS and Azure's government clouds.

title: Microsoft’s PostgreSQL alternative, HorizonDB: Worth the wait?
blurb: Microsoft's HorizonDB, its cloud-native PostgreSQL alternative built on disaggregated compute and storage, has sat in public preview for nine months with no GA date, even as AWS Aurora, Google AlloyDB, Databricks Lakebase, and Snowflake Postgres already ship AI-ready Postgres services. Analysts argue CIOs with urgent AI workloads have little reason to wait, since an undefined GA, pricing, and support roadmap makes mission-critical planning impossible. Azure-committed shops staging new AI projects are the narrow exception.

title: Microsoft Entra ID has a big change coming for Windows Hello for Business and macOS PSSO
blurb: Microsoft is updating Entra ID so Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO can serve as standalone MFA factors rather than only unlocking a separate credential. Enterprises get phishing-resistant MFA already tied to the device, cutting reliance on separate authenticator apps or hardware keys and simplifying Conditional Access policies across mixed Windows and Mac fleets.

title: Serving the most critical missions: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status
blurb: Cloudflare for Government reached FedRAMP High authorization, sponsored by NIST, and is now pursuing DoD Impact Level 4 for controlled unclassified data.

title: Metabase Patches Vulnerability Exploited as Zero-Day
blurb: Metabase released urgent patches for a critical SQL injection flaw that was exploited in the wild as a zero-day, letting remote, unauthenticated attackers gain admin access, steal connected-database credentials, and export data. Metabase Cloud instances are already patched, but self-hosters must update to versions 63.5, 62.9, 61.11, 60.17, 59.21, or 58.24, or block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint as a temporary workaround.

title: ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE: Balancing control and autonomy for your microservices
blurb: Google added ClusterNetworkPolicy to GKE, a cluster-wide resource from the Kubernetes SIG-Policy Working Group that lets platform teams enforce non-bypassable network guardrails above standard namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy. Its three-tier hierarchy (admin, network policy, baseline) evaluates top-to-bottom and maps to RBAC roles, so admins can pin compliance rules and set a default deny-all posture while developers still write their own app policies without overriding core mandates.

title: OpenAI adds technology to compete for ad dollars
blurb: OpenAI added product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to ChatGPT, giving performance marketers the ad formats and conversion tracking they need to treat it as a measurable channel rather than an experiment. The moves position ChatGPT to compete with Google and Meta for performance budgets, where attribution and shoppable placements are the price of entry for anything beyond test spend.

title: Signed up for Klaviyo? Dozens of advertisers may have seen your password
blurb: Klaviyo left its sign-up form misconfigured from at least February 2024 through November 2025, leaking new customers' email addresses and plaintext passwords to third-party trackers from Google, Meta, Microsoft, LinkedIn, HubSpot, and X. The incident, disclosed by researcher Sam Jadali ahead of a Def Con talk, is a reminder that marketing pixels can quietly exfiltrate any data entered on the pages they sit on.

title: Evolve your marketing with new AI tools
blurb: Google announced new agentic capabilities across Google Ads and Google Analytics, including Ask Advisor insights on both homepages, AI Overviews that summarize performance shifts since your last login, and prompt-driven Dashboards that turn raw data into visualizations with a text query. The shift pushes analysis and campaign decisions into in-product AI agents, changing how demand-gen teams monitor impression share and act on demand spikes.

title: A Fresh Definition of The Product Role
blurb: Marty Cagan of SVPG argues that the best recent definition of the product manager role came from an unlikely source: a Benedict Evans piece that barely mentions the word "product." Evans' point is that even as customers gain tools to build their own solutions through vibe-coding and agents, most people don't want to be tool builders, which is exactly the gap the PM role exists to fill. Cagan also treats "how do you define the product role" as an interview Rorschach test, since the answer reveals which operating model a candidate actually worked in.

title: World Liberty received $100 million from businessman investigated for money laundering: NYT
blurb: The New York Times reported that World Liberty Financial received $100 million from Guren "Bobby" Zhou, a businessman under an active British money-laundering investigation as of late July. Zhou has not been charged, but the disclosure adds to scrutiny of the Trump-affiliated DeFi venture's fundraising and the sources behind its treasury.

title: Brazil to tighten crypto fraud controls with new 24-hour wait on transfers to self-custody wallets
blurb: Brazil's central bank will require a 24-hour hold on crypto transfers from exchanges to self-custody wallets starting Jan. 1, 2027, covering fiat-backed stablecoins alongside other tokens. The delay targets scam-driven withdrawals by giving institutions a window to flag fraudulent transfers, but adds friction for users moving assets off regulated platforms.

title: Crypto exchange Coinsbuy loses $8 million in coordinated two-blockchain attack
blurb: Crypto exchange Coinsbuy lost $8.07 million on Aug. 9 when an attacker drained TRON and Ethereum wallets in under an hour, with onchain researchers linking both chains into a single operation through cross-chain swapper Bridgers. Roughly 79% of the funds moved through FixedFloat across 50 single-use addresses, and Coinsbuy refilled the wallets within 24 hours from its own reserves, saying no client bore any loss.

title: North Korea’s Kimsuky integrates AI into cyberattacks targeting crypto and finance
blurb: North Korea's Kimsuky hacking group is running local LLMs via Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty to generate crypto-themed phishing documents and automate malware development, according to a report from South Korean security firm Genians. The offline setup supports retrieval-augmented generation without leaking queries to cloud providers, and follows a year in which North Korean actors stole $2.02B in crypto, including the $1.5B Bybit hack.

title: Bitmine’s ETH buying slows as Tom Lee's firm shifts capital to share buybacks
blurb: Bitmine Immersion (BMNR) bought just 7,391 ETH last week, worth about $14.2 million, its smallest weekly purchase of 2026 as the largest Ethereum treasury firm nears its target of 5% of ETH supply. The firm redirected capital to repurchase 3 million of its own shares for an estimated $50 million to $58 million, part of 19.1 million shares bought back since July.

title: Why the UK financial watchdog is drafting new rules for tokenized gold
blurb: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority is drafting rules for tokenized gold as part of a digital asset strategy to defend London's lead in global bullion trading, where it handles 70% of notional volume. The regulator is consulting financial institutions on using tokenized gold as collateral in wholesale markets, with progress on the rules expected within the next few months as China's share grows.

title: Bitcoin miner Bitdeer’s shares sink 15% despite revenue growth, progress on AI pivot
blurb: Bitdeer's shares fell over 15% on Monday despite Q2 revenue climbing 47% year-over-year to $229 million and Bitcoin production rising nearly 400% to 2,694 BTC. The miner posted a $92.3 million net loss as electricity, depreciation, and interest costs rose, and it held just 150 BTC at quarter-end after selling most of its newly mined coins.

title: Adam Back-backed H100 more than triples bitcoin holdings to 3,506 BTC in acquisition deal
blurb: H100 Group, the Swedish bitcoin treasury firm backed by Blockstream CEO Adam Back, more than tripled its holdings to 3,506 BTC (worth roughly $226.7 million) after acquiring Norwegian firms Moonshot and PDI. The all-stock deal issued 790.5 million new shares for a roughly 70% dilution, moving H100 to the 26th-largest public corporate bitcoin holder even as Strategy and MARA trim their treasuries.

title: Grayscale quietly drops Cardano, Polkadot and Hedera ETF plans
blurb: Grayscale asked the SEC to withdraw its Cardano, Polkadot and Hedera ETF registrations in three sponsor-initiated filings submitted late Friday, ending plans for the single-token products without any securities being issued. The withdrawals track steep drawdowns since the February 2025 filings, with ADA down roughly 70%, DOT down 80% and HBAR down more than 70% over that stretch.

title: Crypto lost $110 million to hacks in July amid rising bug bounty activity: Immunefi
blurb: Crypto lost roughly $110 million to hacks in July, according to security platform Immunefi, which said its audit competitions caught more critical bugs than tier-1 audits over the same period. The findings add to the case that competitive, crowdsourced review is outpacing traditional one-off audits as protocols weigh where to spend limited security budgets.

title: Michael Saylor’s Strategy sells another 1,690 BTC as USD reserve hits $4.65 billion
blurb: Strategy sold another 1,690 BTC, reducing its holdings as its USD reserve reached $4.65 billion. The company still holds roughly 4% of the 21 million bitcoin supply cap, worth about $55 billion, keeping it the largest corporate holder despite the trimmed position.

title: Bitmine adds 7,391 ether in a week, bringing total Ethereum holdings to 5.81 million ETH
blurb: Bitmine Immersion Technologies bought 7,391 ETH over the past week, lifting its treasury to 5,805,238 ETH, or 4.8% of circulating supply, and making it the largest corporate ether holder at roughly $11 billion. Of that, 5.07 million ETH is staked through its MAVAN platform and partners for a projected $257 million in annualized staking revenue.

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to main UK app through Bitstamp
blurb: Robinhood began rolling out crypto trading to eligible UK customers through Bitstamp, the exchange it acquired for $200M last year, adding more than 50 assets including BTC, ETH, XRP, and HYPE to its main investing app. The service launches with zero trading, account, and custody fees, though a 0.1% FX fee applies, and external crypto transfers are not available at launch.

title: ‘Owning the rails’: Standard Chartered sees LINK at $200 by 2030 as Chainlink underpins tokenized-asset boom
blurb: Standard Chartered initiated coverage of Chainlink's LINK with a $200 end-2030 price target, a roughly 25-fold gain from about $8 today, framing the network as core infrastructure for tokenized real-world assets. The bank projects Chainlink's fees scaling about 25 times as onchain tokenized assets climb to $4 trillion by end-2028 from roughly $340 billion now, citing its $110 billion in total value secured.

title: Bitcoin’s BIP-110 supporters split onto minority chain as main network pulls ahead
blurb: Bitcoin's chain split at block 961,632 on Saturday when nodes enforcing BIP-110, a one-year rule restricting non-financial data like Ordinals inscriptions, began rejecting blocks that didn't signal support for the proposal. Only 2.53% of blocks signaled support over the prior two weeks, and the minority fork fell seven blocks behind the main chain within hours as it failed to attract meaningful mining power.

title: Solana gets its first Strategy STRC product through Solstice Finance
blurb: Solstice Finance launched strcUSX on Solana, the first product giving DeFi users structured exposure to the income and price risk of Strategy's STRC preferred stock without tokenizing the underlying shares. Deposited USX splits into a senior token targeting 7% annual yield and a junior token targeting over 20% APY, with junior holders absorbing losses first if STRC's price falls.

title: Bitcoin volatility is in meltdown, but downside protection still commands a premium
blurb: Bitcoin's BVIV implied volatility index fell to 35.59% over the weekend, its lowest since September and down from above 90% in February, as demand for directional options collapsed and miners and corporates kept selling through overwriting strategies. Puts still trade at a premium to calls despite the range-bound $62,000 to $66,000 price, signaling traders remain willing to pay up for downside protection even as overall hedging demand evaporates.

title: Solana lending giant Jupiter now lets the same dollar earn twice
blurb: Jupiter released Lend v2 on Monday, letting deposits and borrowed positions on Solana double as trading liquidity so the same capital earns lending interest plus a share of swap fees. Optional Smart Collateral and Smart Debt features auto-pair assets into correlated pools, but yields depend on Jupiter's router sending enough swap flow, and collateral providers bear the loss if a stablecoin in the pair depegs.

title: Strategy sells 1,690 bitcoin, raises $653 million from MSTR shares
blurb: Strategy sold 1,690 bitcoin for $108.6 million and raised another $653.1 million through the sale of 6.59 million MSTR common shares, directing $650 million to a USD reserve that now sits at $4.65 billion. The bitcoin sales cut its holdings to 840,447 BTC and funded a $108.6 million buyback of variable-rate STRC preferred shares, a shift toward cash and equity management over pure accumulation.

title: World Liberty received $100 million from businessman investigated for money laundering: NYT
blurb: The New York Times reported that World Liberty Financial, the Trump-affiliated crypto venture, received $100 million from Guren "Bobby" Zhou, a businessman under active British investigation for money laundering. Zhou has not been charged, but British officials told the Times the probe remained open as of late July, adding to scrutiny of the vetting behind World Liberty's high-value backers.

title: Brazil to tighten crypto fraud controls with new 24-hour wait on transfers to self-custody wallets
blurb: Brazil will require a 24-hour holding period on crypto transfers from exchanges to self-custody wallets starting Jan. 1, 2027, covering fiat-backed stablecoins as part of a new anti-fraud regime. The delay gives platforms and victims a window to flag and reverse scam-driven withdrawals, but it adds settlement friction that stablecoin and payments operators serving Brazilian users will need to design around.

title: SEC Exempts Data-Center Bonds From Key Securitization Rules
blurb: The SEC exempted data-center asset-backed securities from key securitization rules, making it easier for data-center owners to sell debt to fund the buildout of AI compute capacity. The carve-out lowers the compliance burden on a fast-growing corner of the ABS market, clearing a path for tech firms and their financing partners to raise more structured debt against server-farm assets.

title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda Taps Loans for Nvidia-Tied Chip Deal
blurb: Lambda, the Nvidia-backed AI cloud provider, is selling a leveraged loan to finance a chip purchase, pushing the buildout into the riskier corners of the debt market. The deal signals that AI infrastructure spending has outrun equity and vendor financing, with leveraged loans now a growing funding channel for compute-hungry providers stretching to secure Nvidia GPUs.

title: Sources: Palmer Luckey's Erebor, which aims to fill the gap left by Silicon Valley Bank's collapse, is in advanced talks to raise ~$1.5B at an $8B valuation (Financial Times)
blurb: Erebor, the digital bank founded by Palmer Luckey to serve startups after Silicon Valley Bank's 2023 collapse, is in advanced talks to raise ~$1.5B at an $8B valuation, per the Financial Times. The round would give the crypto- and defense-focused lender a valuation rivaling established sponsor banks, betting that demand for a dedicated startup bank persists two years after SVB's failure.

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to main UK app through Bitstamp
blurb: Robinhood began rolling out crypto trading to eligible UK customers this week through Bitstamp, the FCA-registered exchange it acquired for $200M last year, adding more than 50 assets alongside stocks, ISAs, options, and futures in its main app. The service launches with zero trading, account, and custody fees, though external crypto transfers are unavailable at launch and UK holdings are not covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

title: The Deluge of AI Debt Has Big Names Seeking New Strategies to Avoid Selloffs
blurb: BlackRock structured its financing of Meta's AI data-center buildout to deter fast-trading investors, part of a broader push by big underwriters to manage a flood of AI-related debt hitting credit markets. As issuers stack tens of billions in bonds and private credit to fund compute expansion, banks and asset managers are engineering new deal structures to keep spreads stable and head off a selloff.

title: Podcast: AI Distribution for 5000+ Banks, with Fiserv Co-Head of Financial Solutions Srini Krish
blurb: Fiserv is embedding AI into the technology backbone it provides to 5,000+ US banks and credit unions, packaging models from OpenAI and Anthropic into its Agent OS platform so smaller institutions can compete with JPMorgan and Wells Fargo. The rollout starts with non-real-time, human-in-the-loop cases like commercial loan underwriting, on the logic that money demands deterministic outputs and Fiserv's real moat is distribution rather than direct model access.

title: FCA selects five fintechs to support its Scale-up Unit
blurb: The FCA selected five UK fintechs (ClearScore, Modulr, Teya, Urban Jungle, and Zilch) for the latest cohort of its Scale-up Unit, the first group regulated solely by the FCA to receive dedicated scaleup support spanning payments, consumer credit, credit scoring, and insurtech. The regulator paired the announcement with pilot findings arguing that early investment in regulatory risk and control frameworks is critical to sustainable growth.

title: Why the UK financial watchdog is drafting new rules for tokenized gold
blurb: The FCA is drafting rules for tokenized gold and consulting financial institutions on how bullion-backed tokens could serve as collateral in wholesale markets, with progress expected within months. The move is part of a broader UK push to digitize wholesale markets, projected to add £33B in annual output, as London defends its 70% share of global gold trading against rising competition from China.
